name: Apollo People Search
description: Apollo.io people/prospect search — find contacts across 230M+ people by title, seniority, keywords, location, or employer domain. Keyless x402 via the monid gateway (no API key). Returns matches with an Apollo person id but OBFUSCATED names and NO email — chain Apollo People Enrich (by id) to reveal the real name + verified email.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"apollo","endpoint":"/mixed_people/api_search","input":{"queryParams":{...}}}. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY; put Apollo's search filters under input.queryParams.
usage.outputShape: data.output.{total_entries, people[].{id, first_name, last_name_obfuscated, title, has_email, has_direct_phone, organization{name,...}}}. Names are OBFUSCATED and there is NO email in search — pass person id to Apollo People Enrich.
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}; Apollo's own params go under input.queryParams. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim — do not change them.
Array filters use a [] suffix in the key name: person_titles[], person_seniorities[], person_locations[], q_organization_domains_list[], organization_locations[].

person_seniorities[] vocabulary (use THESE, not free text): owner, founder, c_suite, partner, vp, head, director, manager, senior, entry, intern. Prefer seniority over exact title — title-only filters often return empty.
Filter to an employer with q_organization_domains_list[] (bare domains, no www/@).
Last names are OBFUSCATED (last_name_obfuscated) and there is no email — to de-obfuscate + get the verified email, pass each person id to Apollo People Enrich.
per_page controls result count; paginate with page.
usage.guide: Apollo people search via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.01 on Base). Send body {provider:'apollo', endpoint:'/mixed_people/api_search', input:{queryParams:{...}}}. Filter by person_seniorities[] (owner|founder|c_suite|partner|vp|head|director|manager|senior|entry|intern — prefer seniority over exact person_titles[], which often returns empty), q_organization_domains_list[] (employer domains), person_locations[], q_keywords. Read data.output.people[] — names are obfuscated and there's NO email in search, so pass each person id to Apollo People Enrich to reveal real name + verified email. If a query returns empty, broaden the seniority set / drop the title filter before repeating.

name: Apollo People Enrich
description: Apollo.io people enrichment — resolve a known person into a full profile with VERIFIED work email, title, seniority, employment history, and current employer. Accepts any identifier (Apollo person id from People Search, email, name+domain, or LinkedIn URL). Keyless x402 via the monid gateway. This is the step that reveals the contact data People Search withholds.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"apollo","endpoint":"/people/match","input":{"queryParams":{...}}}. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY; put ONE person identifier under input.queryParams.
usage.outputShape: data.output.person.{id, first_name, last_name, name, title, seniority, email, linkedin_url, employment_history[], organization{...}}.
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}; the person identifier goes under input.queryParams. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim.
Provide at least ONE identifier: id (from People Search — best), email, name+domain, first_name+last_name+organization_name, or linkedin_url. More identifiers improve the match.
Pairs with Apollo People Search: pass the search-result person id here to de-obfuscate the name and get the verified email.
reveal_personal_emails:true surfaces personal emails (paid modifier, +1 credit).
usage.guide: Apollo people enrichment via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.05 on Base). Send body {provider:'apollo', endpoint:'/people/match', input:{queryParams:{ id | email | name+domain | linkedin_url }}}. Best after Apollo People Search: pass the returned person id to reveal the real name + verified work email. Read data.output.person for the full profile.

name: Apollo Org Search
description: Apollo.io organization/company search over 30M+ companies — qualify target accounts by headcount, HQ location, revenue, funding, keyword tags, or technologies. Keyless x402 via the monid gateway.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"apollo","endpoint":"/mixed_companies/search","input":{"queryParams":{...}}}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim; put params under input.queryParams.
usage.outputShape: data.output.{organizations[].{id,name,website_url,primary_domain,industry,estimated_num_employees,...}, pagination}.
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY (do not change them); put the endpoint's own params under input.<slot>. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key.

Array filters use a [] suffix: q_organization_domains_list[], organization_locations[], organization_num_employees_ranges[] (e.g. '11,50'), q_organization_keyword_tags[]. revenue_range uses revenue_range[min]/revenue_range[max].
Returns the Apollo organization_id needed to filter Apollo People Search precisely.
usage.guide: Apollo organization search via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.05 on Base). Body {provider:'apollo', endpoint:'/mixed_companies/search', input:{queryParams:{...}}}. Filter by q_organization_keyword_tags[], organization_locations[], organization_num_employees_ranges[] ('11,50'), revenue_range[min]/[max], currently_using_any_of_technology_uids[]. Read data.output.organizations[] and capture organization id to precisely filter Apollo People Search.

Use to verify a company + get its Apollo organization_id before people search.

name: PDL Person Enrich (monid)
description: People Data Labs person enrich — resolve a person against ~3B profiles for full career history, emails, and phone. Match by email, phone, name+company, or LinkedIn. Keyless x402 via the monid gateway (alternative to the StableEnrich PDL route).

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"pdl","endpoint":"/v5/person/enrich","input":{"body":{...}}}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim; put params under input.body.
usage.outputShape: data.output.data.{full_name,job_title,emails[],phone_numbers[],linkedin_url,experience[],...}, likelihood.

Provide strong identifiers in input.body: email (best), phone, profile (LinkedIn URL), or name+company. More identifiers → higher match likelihood.
$0.30/call — enrich only resolved people, not speculative lookups.
usage.guide: PDL person enrich via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.30 on Base). Body {provider:'pdl', endpoint:'/v5/person/enrich', input:{body:{ email | profile(linkedin) | name+company }}}. Read data.output.data for the full profile. Pricey — only enrich people you've already identified.

name: Hunter.io Email Finder
description: Find the most likely email address for a person given their name and company domain. Returns the guessed email plus a confidence score and a verification block.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.orth.sh/hunter/v2/email-finder?domain=<domain>&first_name=<first>&last_name=<last> (x402 Base USDC, no body). Provide domain (or company) AND a name (first_name+last_name, or full_name). linkedin_handle also accepted.
usage.outputShape: data.email, data.score (0-100 confidence), data.first_name, data.last_name, data.domain, data.company, data.accept_all (bool), data.position, data.twitter, data.linkedin_url, data.phone_number, data.source_type, data.sources[], data.verification.status (valid/invalid/...), data.verification.date, meta.params
quirks: All query params are individually optional in the schema, but a useful call needs domain (or company) PLUS a name (first_name+last_name, or full_name); company is accepted but domain is strongly preferred
Input is URL query params, not a JSON body (GET)
Returned email may differ from a naive first.last@domain guess (returned collison@stripe.com, not patrick@stripe.com)
Read data.score for confidence and data.verification.status for deliverability; data.accept_all=true means the domain accepts all addresses so a high score is less meaningful
Underlying resource is api.hunter.io/v2/email-finder fronted by the Orthogonal x402 gateway

name: Hunter.io Email Verifier
description: Verify whether an email address is deliverable. Returns a status (valid/invalid/accept_all/webmail/disposable/unknown), a 0-100 score, and detailed SMTP/MX checks plus source citations.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.orth.sh/hunter/v2/email-verifier?email=<email_address> (x402 Base USDC, no body). email is REQUIRED.
usage.outputShape: data.status (valid/invalid/accept_all/webmail/disposable/unknown), data.score (0-100), data.email, data.regexp, data.gibberish, data.disposable, data.webmail, data.mx_records, data.smtp_server, data.smtp_check, data.accept_all, data.block, data.sources[]{domain,uri,extracted_on,last_seen_on,still_on_page}, data.result (DEPRECATED), data._deprecation_notice, meta.params

Input is a URL query param, not a JSON body (GET)
Read data.status and data.score; data.result exists but is DEPRECATED per the response's own data._deprecation_notice ('use status instead')
data.sources[] can be very large (verified response was ~4.7KB with ~25 source entries)

name: Nyne Person Enrichment
description: Async person enrichment: given an email, phone, social profile URL, or name+company, returns a rich person profile (name, bio, location, emails/phones, social profiles, organizations, schools, birthday, interests).

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/person/enrichment with JSON body requiring at least one of {email | phone | social_media_url} (or {name + company}). Optional: ai_enhanced_search, strict_email_check, lite_enrich (3 credits vs 6), probability_score, newsfeed[] (linkedin/twitter/instagram/github/facebook/all), callback_url (webhook). Returns 202 {data.status:'queued', data.request_id}. Poll FREE GET https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/person/enrichment?request_id=<id> until data.status=='completed'.
usage.outputShape: data.status, data.request_id, data.completed, data.created_on, data.completed_on, data.result.{firstname,lastname,displayname,gender,bio,location,hometown,timezone,address,url,website,birthday.{year,month,day},best_personal_email,best_work_email,altemails[],fullphone,domains[],organizations[],schools_attended[],schools_info[],interests[],platforms[],possible_matches[],social_profiles.{twitter,linkedin,instagram,tiktok,reddit,github,...}.url}
quirks: Async: paid POST returns HTTP 202 with data.status=='queued' + data.request_id, NOT the result.
Poll the result with a FREE GET to ?request_id=<id> (no payment for polling). Completed in ~20s in this test.
Requires at least one of email, phone, or social_media_url (name needs a company to disambiguate).
Early poll responses return partial result slices and inconsistent key ordering; read the full body once data.status=='completed' / data.completed==true.
social_profiles is a map keyed by platform name (twitter, linkedin, instagram, tiktok, reddit, github, ...) each with a .url (twitter entry also carries posts/media_count/profile_id/username).
lite_enrich=true costs 3 credits instead of 6 and returns only basic fields.

description: Async company enrichment: given a company email, phone, or LinkedIn company URL, returns a company profile (name, description, industry, HQ, employee count, follower count, founding year, logo/background, specialities).

Returns 202 {data.status:'queued', data.request_id}. Poll FREE GET https://x402.orth.sh/nyne/company/enrichment?request_id=<id> until data.status=='completed'.
usage.outputShape: data.status, data.request_id, data.created_on, data.completed_on, data.result.{name,universal_name,linkedin_url,linkedin_id,description,tagline,industry,website_url,founded_on,employee_count,employee_count_range.{start,end},follower_count,headquarter.{street1,city,geographic_area,country},logo_url,background_url,specialities[],last_scraped,updated_on}

name: Minerva Resolve
description: Minerva identity resolution — match a person to a unique Minerva PID + LinkedIn URL, by name+contact or reverse-lookup from email/phone alone. Keyless x402 via StableEnrich.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/resolve with JSON {records:[{record_id, first_name?, last_name?, emails?:[...], phones?:[...]}]}
usage.outputShape: body.results[].{record_id, is_match, minerva_pid, linkedin_url, match_score}
quirks: Input is a `records` ARRAY (batch). Each needs a record_id you choose. Supports reverse lookup by emails/phones only (no name).
Use match_condition_fields:["linkedin_url"] to only return matches that have a LinkedIn profile.
Feed the returned minerva_pid into Minerva Enrich for full data.
usage.guide: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/resolve with {"records":[{"record_id":"u1","first_name":"...","last_name":"...","emails":["..."]}]}. Keyless x402 (~$0.02 on Base). Read body.results[] — each gives minerva_pid + linkedin_url + match_score. Pass the pid to Minerva Enrich for demographics/work/contact data.

name: Minerva Enrich
description: Minerva person enrichment — demographics, work history, education, emails/phones, address history, financial signals. Lookup by Minerva PID, LinkedIn URL, or name/email/phone. Keyless x402 via StableEnrich.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/enrich with JSON {records:[{record_id, minerva_pid?|linkedin_url?|(first_name,last_name,emails)}], return_fields?:[...]}
usage.outputShape: body.results[].{record_id, is_match, minerva_pid, full_name, work_experience, personal_emails, phones, ...}
quirks: Input is a `records` ARRAY. Three lookup modes per record: minerva_pid (fastest), linkedin_url, or name/email/phone.
Use return_fields to limit response size; match_condition_fields to only return records that have specific data.
Best after Minerva Resolve (use its minerva_pid).
usage.guide: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/enrich with {"records":[{"record_id":"u1","minerva_pid":"..."}],"return_fields":[...]}. Keyless x402 (~$0.05 on Base). Read body.results[] for demographics, work history, emails/phones, address + financial signals. Use a minerva_pid from Minerva Resolve for best results.

name: Minerva Validate Emails
description: Minerva email validation — check if email addresses exist in the Minerva identity graph + last-seen timestamps. Cheap pre-screen before resolve/enrich. Keyless x402 via StableEnrich.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/validate-emails with JSON {records:["email1", "email2", ...]}
usage.outputShape: body.results[].{email_address, is_match, email_validation_status, email_last_seen}
quirks: Input `records` is an array of plain email STRINGS (not objects).
Cheapest Minerva op — use it to pre-screen a list before paying for resolve/enrich.
usage.guide: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/minerva/validate-emails with {"records":["a@x.com","b@y.com"]}. Keyless x402 (~$0.01 on Base). Read body.results[] — each gives email_validation_status + last-seen. Use to pre-screen emails before the pricier resolve/enrich.

name: Clado Contacts Enrich (StableEnrich)
description: Clado contact enrichment — get personal email/phone from a LinkedIn URL, email, or phone. Fallback when Apollo lacks personal contacts. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/clado/contacts-enrich with JSON body containing exactly one of {linkedin_url|email|phone}
usage.outputShape: body.data[0].social[] (array of {link,type,rating}); body.data[0].contacts[] (personal email/phone when available); body.data[0].error (bool)
quirks: contacts[] may be empty even on a successful 200 (no personal email/phone found for that subject); social[] is the primary populated result
result wrapped in a top-level data[] array — read body.data[0]
usage.guide: POST to https://stableenrich.dev/api/clado/contacts-enrich with a JSON body holding exactly one identifier: {linkedin_url}, {email}, or {phone}. Pay x402 (~$0.20 USDC on Base), synchronous. Read the result at body.data[0]: contacts[] holds personal email/phone when found, social[] holds matched social profiles ({link,type,rating}). Note contacts[] can be empty on a valid 200.

name: Whitepages Person Search
description: Whitepages person search — find people by name, phone, or address (consumer identity, aliases, phones, properties). Keyless x402 via StableEnrich.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/whitepages/person-search with JSON {first_name, last_name, state_code} (or phone, or address)
usage.outputShape: body.persons[].{id, name, aliases, phones, owned_properties, date_of_birth, company_name, ...}
quirks: Pricey ($0.44/call). State field is `state_code` (two-letter), not `state`.
Searchable by name+state, phone, or address.
usage.guide: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/whitepages/person-search with {"first_name":"...","last_name":"...","state_code":"CA"} (or a phone/address). Keyless x402 (~$0.44 on Base — pricey). Read body.persons[] for matches with aliases, phones, owned properties.

name: Whitepages Property Search
description: Whitepages property search — get property ownership, resident, and property details by address. Keyless x402 via StableEnrich.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/whitepages/property-search with JSON {street, city, state_code}
usage.outputShape: body.result.{property_id, apn, property_address, owners, residents, ...}
quirks: Pricey ($0.44/call). The state field MUST be `state_code` (two-letter, e.g. 'CA') — using `state` is silently ignored and breaks the lookup.
Returns a single body.result object (not an array).
usage.guide: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/whitepages/property-search with {"street":"...","city":"...","state_code":"CA"}. Keyless x402 (~$0.44 on Base — pricey). Read body.result for property ownership/resident/APN details. Use state_code (two-letter), never state.

name: FullEnrich People Search
description: FullEnrich people search — find people by company domain/name/LinkedIn, seniority, title, location, skills. First-class people discovery (replaces Apollo). $0.14 when results, free when empty; ≤10 per query, paginate with search_after. Email is NOT in results — chain PDL people-enrich for emails/phone.

usage.callShape: POST /api/fullenrich/people-search with JSON filters (each value as {value:...})
usage.outputShape: JSON body (see StableEnrich OpenAPI).
usage.guide: FullEnrich people search. Filter by current_company_domains, current_position_seniority_level (C-level|VP|Head|Founder — not Apollo values), current_position_titles, person_locations, person_skills. ≥1 filter required (offset alone → 400). 3+ filters often returns zero — start with domain+seniority. ≤10 results/query; paginate via metadata.search_after. Free on no match. For emails/phone, chain to PDL people-enrich by profile/email.

name: FullEnrich Company Search
description: FullEnrich company search — find companies by name/industry/HQ/headcount/domain. Verify a company domain before people searches. $0.14 when results, free when empty; ≤10 per query, paginate with search_after.

usage.callShape: POST /api/fullenrich/company-search with ≥1 of names|industries|headquarters_locations (each value as {value:...})
usage.outputShape: JSON body (see StableEnrich OpenAPI).
usage.guide: FullEnrich company search. Provide names, industries (exact FullEnrich enum — AI cos index under Research Services, not Artificial Intelligence), headquarters_locations, or domains. page/offset alone → 400. Search by legal entity not brand. ≤10 results; paginate via metadata.search_after (page is ignored on cache hits). Free on no match.

name: CompanyEnrich Org Enrich
description: CompanyEnrich organization enrich — full company profile by domain (employees/revenue as range strings, funding array, socials). Verify the returned domain before downstream people searches. $0.06.

usage.callShape: POST /api/companyenrich/org-enrich {domain}
usage.outputShape: JSON body (see StableEnrich OpenAPI).
usage.guide: CompanyEnrich org-enrich {domain} → firmographics. employees/revenue are RANGE strings (don t numeric-compare). Known bad resolves: openai.com → wrong entity; x.com → 404 (use twitter.com). M&A not in funding. Use to verify a company domain before FullEnrich people-search.

name: CompanyEnrich Properties Enrich
description: CompanyEnrich properties enrich — company profile by name or social URL when the domain is unknown (best-match; verify returned domain). $0.06.

usage.callShape: POST /api/companyenrich/properties-enrich {name} or {linkedinUrl}
usage.outputShape: JSON body (see StableEnrich OpenAPI).
usage.guide: CompanyEnrich properties-enrich {name} or {linkedinUrl} when you lack a domain (best-match — verify returned domain before trusting). employees/revenue are range strings. Prefer org-enrich {domain} when you have a domain.

name: PDL People Enrich
description: People Data Labs person enrich — full career history, emails, and phone. Best after a people-search: enrich by LinkedIn profile or email. $0.28 per match, free on no-match (HTTP 200, data:null).

usage.callShape: POST /api/pdl/people-enrich with one of {email} | {profile} | {first_name+last_name+company_domain}
usage.outputShape: JSON body (see StableEnrich OpenAPI).
usage.guide: PDL people-enrich. Prefer {email}, else {profile} (LinkedIn URL), else {first_name,last_name,company_domain}. {first_name,last_name} alone → 400. No match → HTTP 200 {status:404,data:null}, NOT billed. Returns career history, emails, phone. Use as the enrich step after FullEnrich people-search resolves LinkedIn URLs.

name: Apollo Get Complete Person
description: Apollo.io — direct lookup of everything Apollo knows about one person by their Apollo person id: name, title, verified email, employment history, and location. Keyless x402 via the monid gateway.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"apollo","endpoint":"/people/{id}","input":{"pathParams":{...}}}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim; put params under input.pathParams.
usage.outputShape: data.output.person.{id,first_name,last_name,name,title,email,linkedin_url,employment_history[],organization{...}}.
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY (do not change them); put the endpoint's own params under input.<slot>. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key.
The Apollo person id goes in input.pathParams.id — the gateway fills the {id} in the endpoint path.
Use the id returned by Apollo People Search.
usage.guide: Apollo person lookup by id via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.05 on Base). Body {provider:'apollo', endpoint:'/people/{id}', input:{pathParams:{id:'...'}}}. Use the person id from Apollo People Search; read data.output.person.

name: Apollo Get Complete Organization

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"apollo","endpoint":"/organizations/{id}","input":{"pathParams":{...}}}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim; put params under input.pathParams.
usage.outputShape: data.output.organization.{id,name,website_url,industry,estimated_num_employees,annual_revenue,funding_events[],technology_names[],...}.
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY (do not change them); put the endpoint's own params under input.<slot>. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key.
The Apollo organization id goes in input.pathParams.id.
Use the id from Apollo Org Search / Org Enrich.
usage.guide: Apollo organization lookup by id via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.05 on Base). Body {provider:'apollo', endpoint:'/organizations/{id}', input:{pathParams:{id:'...'}}}. Read data.output.organization.

Match by ONE of website (best), name, profile (LinkedIn), or ticker — in input.body.
usage.guide: PDL company enrich via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.10 on Base). Body {provider:'pdl', endpoint:'/v5/company/enrich', input:{body:{website:'...'}}}. Read data.output for firmographics.

name: PDL Company Search (monid)
description: People Data Labs company search — filter the full PDL company dataset by firmographics via an Elasticsearch query. Keyless x402 via the monid gateway.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"pdl","endpoint":"/v5/company/search","input":{"body":{...}}}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim; put params under input.body.
usage.outputShape: data.output.data[].{name,website,industry,employee_count,location{...}}, total.
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY (do not change them); put the endpoint's own params under input.<slot>. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key.
Provide an Elasticsearch query object under input.body.query (Elasticsearch recommended over SQL; provide one, not both). size caps results.
Advanced: prefer Apollo Org Search for simple firmographic filters.
usage.guide: PDL company search via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.10 on Base). Body {provider:'pdl', endpoint:'/v5/company/search', input:{body:{query:<elasticsearch>, size:N}}}. For simple filters, Apollo Org Search is easier.

usage.outputShape: data.output — LinkedIn company people list (profiles, headlines, titles); paginate with page.

page paginates (default 1).
usage.guide: TikHub LinkedIn company people via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.006 on Base). Body {provider:'tikhub', endpoint:'/api/v1/linkedin/web/get_company_people', input:{queryParams:{company_id:'...', page:1}}}. Resolve company_id via TikHub LinkedIn Company Profile first.

name: TikHub LinkedIn People Search

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"tikhub","endpoint":"/api/v1/linkedin/web/search_people","input":{"queryParams":{...}}}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim; put params under input.queryParams.
usage.outputShape: data.output — LinkedIn people search results (name, headline, title, company).
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY (do not change them); put the endpoint's own params under input.<slot>. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key.
Filter by name, first_name, last_name, title, current_company/company, industry, geocode_location, school; page paginates.
usage.guide: TikHub LinkedIn people search via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.006 on Base). Body {provider:'tikhub', endpoint:'/api/v1/linkedin/web/search_people', input:{queryParams:{title:'...', current_company:'...', page:1}}}.

description: TikHub — LinkedIn company profile (industry, size, description, and the LinkedIn company_id) by company name. Keyless x402 via the monid gateway.

usage.outputShape: data.output — LinkedIn company profile incl. company_id, industry, staff count, description.

Provide company (name) OR company_id (at least one). The returned company_id feeds TikHub LinkedIn Company People.
usage.guide: TikHub LinkedIn company profile via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.006 on Base). Body {provider:'tikhub', endpoint:'/api/v1/linkedin/web/get_company_profile', input:{queryParams:{company:'...'}}}. Use the returned company_id for TikHub LinkedIn Company People.

name: Apify LinkedIn Company Employees
description: Apify (HarvestAPI) — mass-scrape LinkedIn company employees at scale with filters (title, seniority, location) and optional email discovery + SMTP validation. Priced per result. Keyless x402 via the monid gateway.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.monid.ai/v1/run with body {"provider":"apify","endpoint":"/harvestapi/linkedin-company-employees","input":{"body":{...}}}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key. Copy provider+endpoint verbatim; put params under input.body.
usage.outputShape: data.output — array of employee profiles (name, headline, current/past experience, education, skills; emails when profileScraperMode includes email).
quirks: monid gateway envelope: the request BODY is {provider,endpoint,input}. Copy provider+endpoint EXACTLY (do not change them); put the endpoint's own params under input.<slot>. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key.
PER-RESULT pricing (~$0.018/result + ~$0.02 flat) — the x402 charge scales with maxItems, so keep maxItems small and START with ONE company to gauge cost before fanning out.
Filter with companies[], jobTitles[], seniorityLevelIds[], locations[]. profileScraperMode: 'Short' | 'Full' | 'Full + email' (email discovery costs more).
usage.guide: Apify LinkedIn company-employees via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, per-result ~$0.018 + flat). Body {provider:'apify', endpoint:'/harvestapi/linkedin-company-employees', input:{body:{companies:[...], jobTitles:[...], maxItems:10, profileScraperMode:'Full + email'}}}. Cost SCALES with maxItems — keep it small and prove on one company first. Use 'Full + email' only when you need emails.

usage.outputShape: data.output — matched company identity (uuid, name, website, product_category, company_status).

usage.guide: Akta company search via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.01 on Base). Body {provider:'akta', endpoint:'/v1/company/search', input:{queryParams:{query:'stripe.com'}}}. Read data.output for the company identity + uuid.

usage.guide: Akta industry-code resolution via the monid x402 gateway (keyless, ~$0.01 on Base). Body {provider:'akta', endpoint:'/v1/industry/search', input:{queryParams:{query:'...'}}}.

name: Crustdata Company Search (auor)
description: Search CrustData's company database by firmographic filters (keyword, industry, region, headcount, revenue, growth, funding/leadership signals, hiring) and get back matching companies with name, description, website, LinkedIn URL/id, industry, HQ, employee count + growth, specialties, and estimated revenue range. Keyless x402 via the auor.io (Oreo) gateway.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.auor.io/crustdata/v1/companies/search with a JSON body of firmographic filters (all optional). x402 Base USDC (fixed $0.05), no API key, no body-envelope. Fields: keyword (string), industry (string[]), region (string[]), headcount (string[] of '1-10'|'11-50'|'51-200'|'201-500'|'501-1,000'|'1,001-5,000'|'5,001-10,000'|'10,001+'), followerCount, fortune, accountActivities ('Senior leadership changes in last 3 months'|'Funding events in past 12 months'), jobOpportunities ('Hiring on Linkedin'), headcountGrowth {min,max}, annualRevenue {min,max} (in millions), departmentHeadcount {min,max,department}, currency, page (number).
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object (verified from a live paid 200): { companies: [ { name, description, linkedin_company_url, linkedin_company_id, website, industry, company_type, founded_year, location, headquarters{country, geographicArea, city, postalCode}, employee_count, employee_count_range, employee_growth_percentages[{timespan:'SIX_MONTHS'|'YEAR'|'TWO_YEAR', percentage}], specialties[], revenue_range{estimatedMinRevenue{amount,unit,currencyCode}, estimatedMaxRevenue{...}}, decision_makers_count, logo_urls{'200x200','100x100','400x400'} } ], total_display_count }. The verified call returned 25 companies with total_display_count '32K+'.
quirks: All input fields are optional; a keyword-only body returns results (verified with {keyword:'software', headcount:['51-200']}).
region and industry filter values are NOT free text — they must be pulled from GET /crustdata/v1/filters?type=region and ?type=industry respectively.
headcount / followerCount / fortune / accountActivities / jobOpportunities are fixed enums (see callShape); annualRevenue is in millions.
total_display_count is a formatted STRING (e.g. '32K+'), not an integer count of returned rows; the response returned 25 companies per page — paginate with the `page` field.
Underlying data is CrustData, fronted keylessly by the auor.io (Oreo) x402 gateway; response shape mirrors CrustData's public company shape.
usage.guide: Search CrustData's company database over auor.io's keyless x402 gateway. Issue a POST to https://api.auor.io/crustdata/v1/companies/search with a JSON body of firmographic filters and pay the fixed $0.05 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key). All filters are optional — start with keyword (a company/topic term) and/or headcount (e.g. ['51-200']), and narrow with annualRevenue {min,max} (millions), headcountGrowth {min,max}, departmentHeadcount {min,max,department}, accountActivities ('Funding events in past 12 months'), or jobOpportunities ('Hiring on Linkedin'). For region and industry filters, first fetch the allowed values from GET /crustdata/v1/filters?type=region|industry — they reject free text. Read the synchronous 200 JSON: companies[] gives name, website, linkedin_company_url/id, industry, headquarters, employee_count + employee_growth_percentages, specialties, and revenue_range; total_display_count is a formatted string ('32K+') for the full match set. Page through more results with the `page` field. No polling.

name: NetIntel GitHub Repo Intel
description: Fetches public metadata and an activity/health score for any GitHub repository — stars, forks, watchers, open issues, language breakdown, license, topics, contributor count, latest release, last-commit recency, and a 0-100 score + letter grade — so agents can evaluate dependencies and assess open-source project health without the GitHub API.

repo.description: GitHub repository in owner/repo format (e.g. expressjs/express) or a full GitHub URL. Sent as ?repo=owner/repo on GET or {"repo":"owner/repo"} on POST.

usage.callShape: POST https://netintel.dev/github-intel/analyze with JSON body {"repo":"owner/repo"} (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no API key). GET with ?repo=owner/repo also works.
usage.outputShape: repo, url, description, homepage, stars, forks, watchers, open_issues, primary_language, languages{lang:bytes}, license, license_spdx, topics[], created_at, last_pushed_at, days_since_last_push, is_archived, is_fork, parent_repo, default_branch, contributor_count, latest_release, latest_release_date, score(0-100), grade, findings[].{rule,deduction,detail}
quirks: repo accepts either owner/repo shorthand or a full github.com URL
Result is synchronous — repo metadata + activity/health score returned inline in the 200; no polling
Blocks private/internal targets (SSRF-safe); failed/4xx/5xx calls are never charged (agent fair-trade)
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.03
score is a 0-100 open-source health score with a letter grade (A-F); findings[] lists the scoring rules and deductions applied
usage.guide: Fetches public metadata and an activity/health score for any GitHub repository — stars, forks, watchers, open issues, language breakdown, license, topics, contributor count, latest release, last-commit recency, and a 0-100 score + letter grade — so agents can evaluate dependencies and assess open-source project health without the GitHub API. POST https://netintel.dev/github-intel/analyze with JSON body {"repo":"owner/repo"} (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no API key). GET with ?repo=owner/repo also works. Output: repo, url, description, homepage, stars, forks, watchers, open_issues, primary_language, languages, license, topics, created_at, last_pushed_at, days_since_last_push, contributor_count, latest_release, score(0-100), grade, findings[].

name: Greeneris Swiss Company Lookup
description: Swiss commercial-register lookup via the official Zefix (Federal Office of Justice) index: search companies by name or fetch a full profile by UID or CH-ID, returning legal form, status, canton, seat, purpose, address and official Zefix/cantonal excerpt links, for KYB.

q.description: Company name to search (3+ chars, substring). Returns matches with UID, legal form and status.

uid.description: Swiss UID for the full record, e.g. CHE-105.909.036

chid.description: Swiss CH-ID for the full record, e.g. CH-020.3.926.598-9

canton.description: Filter search by 2-letter canton, e.g. ZH

active_only.description: false = include cancelled companies in search

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/ch/company?q=<NAME> (search) OR ?uid=CHE-... / ?chid=CH-... (full profile)
usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{total_results, results[]{uid, chid, ehraid, name, legal_form, natural_person, status, canton, legal_seat, purpose, capital, address, sogc_date, deletion_date, zefix_url, cantonal_excerpt_url}, hint, source}
quirks: Two modes on one endpoint: name search via ?q= (3+ chars) returns lightweight matches + a hint to call again with uid=; ?uid= or ?chid= returns the full company record (canton, seat, purpose, capital, excerpt links).
Search response trims fields (uid/name/legal_form/status/legal_seat/sogc_date); pass uid to get the full record.
Optional filters: canton (2-letter), active_only (default true — set false to include cancelled companies), limit (1-20, default 5).
Sole-proprietor home addresses are withheld for GDPR.
Results are 24h-cached; static price ($0.005), not a dynamic quote.
legal_form abbreviations appear in search results (e.g. 'PSI') and are spelled out in the OpenAPI example ('Public sector institution').
usage.guide: Look up a Swiss company in the official Zefix commercial register for KYB/due-diligence. Search by name: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/ch/company?q=swisscom (optional canton=ZH, active_only=false, limit=1-20) -> matches with uid/name/legal_form/status. Then fetch the full profile: GET .../v1/ch/company?uid=CHE-102.753.938 (or chid=CH-...) -> canton, seat, purpose, capital, address, and official zefix_url + cantonal_excerpt_url. Output: ok (bool) + data.{total_results, results[], hint, source}. $0.005 USDC on Base per call; 24h cached.

name: Greeneris Czech Company Lookup
description: Czech commercial-register lookup via the official ARES index (Czech Ministry of Finance, ares.gov.cz): search companies by name or fetch by 8-digit ICO, returning ICO, DIC (CZ VAT number, cross-checkable in EU VIES), legal form, registered address, NACE activity codes, per-register status and creation date, for KYB.

q.description: Company name or ICO (8-digit Czech company id), e.g. 'skoda auto' or '00177041'

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/cz/company?q=<NAME or 8-digit ICO> (optional limit=1-10)
usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{total_results, results[]{ico, name, dic, legal_form, natural_person, address{text,city,postal_code,country}, nace_codes[], registrations{ros,vr,res,rzp,dph,sd,...}, date_created, date_dissolved, last_updated}, source}
quirks: Query ?q= accepts either a company name or an 8-digit ICO (Czech company id); returns matches sorted by relevance.
dic is the CZ VAT number (ICO prefixed with 'CZ'), cross-checkable against EU VIES.

registrations is a per-register status map (ros=commercial register, vr=public register, res=economic-subject register, rzp=trade register, dph=VAT, sd=... ) with values like 'AKTIVNI' (active) / 'ZANIKLY' (ceased).
legal_form is a numeric ARES code (e.g. '121' = joint-stock company), not spelled out.
Company data only — personal data of natural persons is stripped for GDPR.
Results are 24h-cached; static price ($0.003), not a dynamic quote.
limit is 1-10 (default 3).
usage.guide: Look up a Czech company in the official ARES commercial register (Czech Ministry of Finance) for KYB/due-diligence. Search by name: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/cz/company?q=skoda%20auto (optional limit=1-10), or by ICO: ?q=00177041. Returns ok (bool) + data.{total_results, results[]{ico, name, dic (CZ VAT), legal_form, address, nace_codes, registrations status map, date_created, date_dissolved, last_updated}, source}. Use dic against EU VIES to confirm VAT. $0.003 USDC on Base per call; 24h cached.

name: Greeneris EU Tenders
description: Fresh EU public procurement notices (leads) from TED (Tenders Electronic Daily, the EU Publications Office API), filterable by CPV code and buyer country, keyless pay-per-call over x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/eu/tenders with optional query params (cpv, country, days_back, limit). One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key, no account. Result returned inline in the 200 body under data.notices[].
usage.outputShape: { ok, data: { query{cpv,country,published_since}, total_matches, notices[]{ publication_number, publication_date, title, buyer_name, deadline (nullable), url }, source } }
quirks: All query params are optional; with no filters it returns the latest EU-wide notices from the last 7 days.
cpv is an 8-digit CPV procurement classification code (e.g. 48000000 = software/IT); country is a 3-letter ISO code, e.g. FRA.
Each notice.url links to the full TED notice on ted.europa.eu; deadline can be null when TED has not published a submission deadline.
1h cache on the upstream TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) source; new notices published daily.
days_back is capped 1-30, limit is capped 1-25.
usage.guide: Use to source fresh EU public-sector procurement opportunities/leads. Narrow by CPV code (sector) and/or 3-letter buyer country, and set days_back (1-30) for freshness and limit (1-25) for volume. Read notices[].url for the full TED notice; buyer_name identifies the contracting authority.

name: Greeneris French Annual Accounts
description: French company annual accounts (bilans) from the official INPI Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), by SIREN - returns the full filing history (closing date, filing date, type complet/simplifie/consolide, public or confidential) plus headline figures (revenue, operating revenue, operating result, total assets, equity) for the latest public filing when the liasse scheme is mapped.

figures.description: Each figure is { n, n_1 } (current year and prior year, amounts in the reported currency, as filed): revenue, operating_revenue, operating_result, total_assets, equity

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/bilans?siren=<9-digit SIREN>. Single required query param siren (Luhn-validated). Pure x402 (Base USDC), no API key - the payment is the auth. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous), no polling. 24h cache.
usage.outputShape: { ok: true, data: { siren, filings_found, filings_returned, filings: [ { closing_date, filed_on, type, type_label (complet/simplifie/consolide/banque), confidentiality (Public/Confidential), updated_at } ], latest: { closing_date, filed_on, type, type_label, months_covered, currency, activity_code, figures: { revenue, operating_revenue, operating_result, total_assets, equity } each as { n, n_1 } }, coverage: { status, fields }, source } }
quirks: Only argument is siren (9 digits). Passing a SIRET (14 digits) or a Luhn-invalid number will fail validation - use the SIREN portion.

Headline figures under latest.figures appear only when INPI's liasse scheme is mapped for that filing; coverage.status may say not_covered (figures omitted) rather than guessing. The filing history is always returned even without figures.
figures values are { n, n_1 } = current-year and prior-year amounts, in the filing's own currency (currency field, e.g. EUR), reported as filed - not audited or restated.
type codes: K=consolide, C=complet, S=simplifie, B=banque; a Confidential filing (confidentiality field) is itself a KYB signal.
method enum also accepts HEAD/DELETE per the OpenAPI schema, but GET is the read call.
24h server-side cache; source is INPI Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), data.inpi.fr.
usage.guide: Provide a 9-digit French SIREN: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/bilans?siren=552032534. If you only have a company name or SIRET, first resolve the SIREN via /v1/fr/company (SIRENE lookup) or take the first 9 digits of the SIRET. Read data.latest.figures for the most recent headline financials (revenue/operating_result/total_assets/equity as n vs n_1) and data.filings for the full history. Each paid call is $0.03 in USDC on Base; the whole result is returned inline.

name: Greeneris French BODACC Legal Announcements

Keyless over x402. $0.01.

outputSchema.description: { ok, data: { siren, famille, total_count, count, announcements: [ { id, date, family, family_code, type, company, legal_form, capital, siren, tribunal, city, departement, judgment, deposit: { type, closing_date }|null, url } ], source } }

usage.callShape: GET /v1/fr/bodacc?siren=<9-digit SIREN>&famille=<family>&limit=<1-20>
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok:true, data:{ siren, famille:null, total_count:47, count:5, announcements:[{ id, date, family, family_code, type, company, legal_form, capital, siren, tribunal, city, departement, judgment, deposit:{ type, closing_date }|null, url }], source } }
quirks: siren is REQUIRED and must be a valid 9-digit French SIREN (Luhn-validated); e.g. 383474814 (AIRBUS).
Zero announcements for a valid SIREN is a clean-record signal (not an error).
famille filters by announcement family; 'collective' = insolvency proceedings, 'dpc' = deposit of accounts, 'vente' = sales/cessions, 'modification' = modifications, 'radiation' = removal.
Legal entities only — GDPR-safe, no natural-person announcements.
Source is DILA BODACC open data (bodacc-datadila.opendatasoft.com, Licence Ouverte), daily publications, cached 1h.
Announcements are newest-first; total_count is the full count, count is how many returned (bounded by limit 1-20, default 10).
usage.guide: French BODACC legal-gazette lookup for KYB / credit-risk. Pass ?siren= a valid 9-digit SIREN (get one from the sibling v1/fr/company registry lookup); optionally filter with famille=collective to isolate insolvency proceedings, and cap results with limit (1-20). Read data.announcements[] for family/family_code, tribunal, judgment and date, plus the official BODACC source url. An empty announcements array for a valid SIREN means a clean record. No API key — pay the x402 402 (Base USDC, $0.01).

outputSchema.description: { ok, data: { total_results, page, results: [ { siren, name, legal_name, naf_code, legal_form, natural_person, company_category, employee_range, creation_date, administrative_status, establishments_total, establishments_open, headquarters: { siret, address, postal_code, city, naf_code }, finances: { <year>: { ca, resultat_net } } } ], source } }

usage.callShape: GET /v1/fr/company?q=<name|SIREN>&per_page=<1-10>&page=<1-50>
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok:true, data:{ total_results, page, results:[{ siren, name, legal_name, naf_code, legal_form, natural_person, company_category, employee_range, creation_date, administrative_status, establishments_total, establishments_open, headquarters:{ siret, address, postal_code, city, naf_code }, finances:{ <year>:{ ca, resultat_net } } }], source } }
quirks: q is REQUIRED and accepts either a company name (e.g. airbus) or a 9-digit SIREN (e.g. 383474814).
Director/officer personal data is stripped for GDPR — this returns company firmographics only, no people.

usage.guide: French KYB registry lookup. Pass ?q= a company name or a 9-digit SIREN; narrow noisy name searches with code_postal, activite_principale (NAF), or etat_administratif=A. Read data.results[] for firmographics (SIREN, legal_form, naf_code, headquarters address, employee_range, administrative_status A/C, finances by year). No API key — pay the x402 402 (Base USDC, $0.005). For a Swiss/UK/etc. company use the sibling v1/ch|uk|... /company endpoints instead.

name: Greeneris FR Tenders
description: Fresh French public procurement notices (leads) from BOAMP (DILA open-data portal, Licence Ouverte), filterable by department code and sector keyword, keyless pay-per-call over x402.

keyword.description: Sector keyword matched against BOAMP descriptors (optional), e.g. informatique

limit.description: Number of notices to return, 1-50 (optional, default 10)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/tenders with optional query params (department, keyword, limit). One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key, no account. Result returned inline in the 200 body under data.tenders[].
usage.outputShape: { ok, data: { query{department,keyword,limit}, total_matches, returned, tenders[]{ idweb, objet, nomacheteur, dateparution, datelimitereponse (nullable), famille_libelle, code_departement[], type_marche[], descripteur_libelle[], url_avis }, source } }
quirks: All query params are optional; with no filters it returns the latest France-wide BOAMP notices, newest first.
department is a French department code as a string, e.g. 59 (Nord), 2A (Corse-du-Sud), 971 (Guadeloupe); keyword is matched against BOAMP sector descriptors, e.g. informatique.
Each tender.url_avis links to the full notice on boamp.fr; datelimitereponse (response deadline) can be null when BOAMP has no submission deadline.
code_departement is an array — a notice can span multiple departments, so a department filter matches any notice listing that code.
limit is capped 1-50 (default 10); 1h cache on the upstream BOAMP (DILA opendatasoft) source, new notices published daily.
Distinct from Greeneris EU Tenders (TED): this is French national BOAMP data only.
usage.guide: Use to source fresh French public-sector procurement opportunities/leads. Narrow by French department code and/or a sector keyword (matched against BOAMP descriptors), and set limit (1-50) for volume. Read tenders[].url_avis for the full BOAMP notice; nomacheteur identifies the contracting authority and datelimitereponse the response deadline.

name: Greeneris LEI Lookup
description: Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) reference data from the GLEIF golden copy (CC0, refreshed daily) - direct lookup by 20-character LEI code, or search by legal name with an optional country filter; returns legal_name, entity/registration status, jurisdiction, legal form, HQ city/country and next renewal date.

lei.description: 20-character LEI code for a direct lookup

name.description: Legal name to search (used when lei is absent)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/global/lei with query params. Two modes: direct lookup ?lei=<20-char LEI> OR name search ?name=<legal name>&country=<2-letter, optional>&limit=<1-10>. Pure x402 (Base USDC), no API key - the payment is the auth. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous), no polling.
usage.outputShape: { ok: true, data: { query, total, results: [ { lei, legal_name, entity_status (e.g. ACTIVE), registration_status (ISSUED/LAPSED), jurisdiction, legal_form_id, hq_city, hq_country, next_renewal_date } ], source } }
quirks: Two query modes on one endpoint: pass ?lei= for a single exact record, or ?name= (plus optional country/limit) for a fuzzy legal-name search returning up to 10 matches.
registration_status of LAPSED means the LEI registration was not renewed - still a real record, just stale; check entity_status (ACTIVE) and next_renewal_date.
Data is the GLEIF LEI golden copy (CC0), refreshed daily with a 24h cache; jurisdiction/country are 2-letter ISO codes.
method enum also accepts HEAD/DELETE per the schema, but GET is the read call.
usage.guide: To resolve an entity you already have the LEI for, call ?lei=529900FCMZ4LKXFD0R69. To find an entity's LEI, search ?name=airbus&country=FR&limit=5 and pick the best match by legal_name + hq_country. Each paid call is $0.005 in USDC on Base; the whole result set is returned inline.

name: Greeneris Irish Company Lookup
description: Irish company-registry lookup via the official CRO open data (opendata.cro.ie, Companies Registration Office daily snapshot): search by company name or CRO company number, returning company number, name, status, type, registration/dissolution dates, registered address, NACE code, and last annual-return/accounts dates, for KYB.

q.description: Company name (full-text search) or CRO company number (digits only), e.g. 'ryanair' or '249885'

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/ie/company?q=<NAME or CRO number>&limit=<1-10>
usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{query, match_mode, total_results, results[]{company_num, name, status, insolvency_signal, company_type, registration_date, dissolution_date, address, eircode, nace_code, last_annual_return_date, next_annual_return_due, last_accounts_date}, source}
quirks: Single ?q= param drives both modes: digits-only is treated as a CRO company number (match_mode=company_num, exact), any other string is a full-text name search (match_mode=name).
limit is 1-10 (default 3).
Some fields are frequently null even for large companies (eircode, nace_code observed null for Ryanair).
insolvency_signal is a convenience boolean flag on each result.
Company data only, no personal data (CC-BY 4.0 CRO open data).
Results are 24h-cached; static price ($0.003), not a dynamic quote.
Source is a daily snapshot of the CRO register (opendata.cro.ie), so it can lag same-day filings.
usage.guide: Look up an Irish company in the official CRO register for KYB/due-diligence. Search by name: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/ie/company?q=ryanair (optional limit=1-10, default 3) -> matches with company_num/name/status/type/address. Or fetch by CRO company number directly: GET .../v1/ie/company?q=249885&limit=1 -> the exact company record with registration/dissolution dates, registered address, NACE code, insolvency_signal, and last annual-return/accounts dates. Output: ok (bool) + data.{query, match_mode, total_results, results[], source}. $0.003 USDC on Base per call; 24h cached.

name: Greeneris LEI Ownership
description: Corporate ownership tree for any Legal Entity Identifier from the official GLEIF LEI graph (CC0): entity name/status plus declared direct parent, ultimate parent and a sample of direct children with the total child count.

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/lei/ownership?lei=<20-char LEI>. Single required query param `lei`. Pure x402 (Base USDC), no API key - the payment is the auth. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous), no polling.
usage.outputShape: { ok: true, data: { lei, found, name, status (e.g. ACTIVE), direct_parent: { lei, name }, ultimate_parent: { lei, name }, children_total, children_sample: [ { lei, name } ] (up to 10), source } } - e.g. lei=549300B56MD0ZC402L06 -> Bloomberg L.P., direct/ultimate parent Bloomberg Inc. (549300RMUDWPHCUQNE66), children_total 27.
quirks: Single required query param `lei` (a 20-character ISO 17442 code); there is no name-search mode here - use /v1/global/lei to resolve a name to an LEI first, then feed the LEI in.
An unknown or invalid LEI returns { ok: true, data: { found: false, ... } } rather than an error - check data.found before trusting the tree.
children_sample is capped at a 10-entity sample; children_total gives the real count (may exceed the sample).
Data is the GLEIF LEI relationship graph (CC0, 2.5M+ entities), served with a 24h cache; direct_parent/ultimate_parent are the entity's own declared parents and may be null when none is reported.
Schema method enum also lists HEAD/DELETE, but GET is the read call.
usage.guide: Map a company's corporate ownership. First get its LEI (via /v1/global/lei name search if you only have a name), then GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/lei/ownership?lei=<LEI>. Response returns the entity's declared direct parent, ultimate parent, and a sample of direct children with the total child count, all from the GLEIF golden-copy graph. No body, no API key - pay $0.005 USDC on Base via x402. Verify data.found is true before using the result.

name: Greeneris Norwegian Company Lookup
description: Norwegian company-registry lookup via the official Brreg Enhetsregisteret (Bronnoysund Register Centre): search companies by name or 9-digit organisation number (orgnr), returning legal form, NACE code, business address, registration date, employees, VAT registration and bankruptcy/liquidation flags, for KYB.

q.description: Company name or 9-digit organisation number (orgnr), e.g. 'equinor' or '923609016'

size.description: Results per page for name search (1-10)

usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{total_results, results[]{orgnr, name, org_form{code,description}, natural_person, nace{code,description}, address{street[],postal_code,city,municipality,country_code}, registration_date, employees, vat_registered, bankrupt, under_liquidation, under_forced_liquidation}, source}
quirks: One required param q accepts either a company name (substring search) or a 9-digit organisation number (orgnr) for an exact lookup.
size (1-10, default 3) caps the number of name-search matches; total_results reports the full match count regardless (e.g. q=equinor -> total_results 240, results trimmed to size).
Data is the official Norwegian Enhetsregisteret via data.brreg.no (Bronnoysund Register Centre), NLOD 2.0 licensed with personal contact data removed.
employees / NACE / address may be absent for some entities; bankruptcy and liquidation flags are always present booleans.
Results are 24h-cached; static price ($0.003), not a dynamic quote.
usage.guide: Look up a Norwegian company in the official Brreg Enhetsregisteret for KYB/due-diligence. Search by name: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/no/company?q=equinor&size=1 -> matches with orgnr, legal form, NACE, address, employees, VAT + bankruptcy/liquidation flags. Or fetch by exact org number: GET .../v1/no/company?q=923609016. Output: ok (bool) + data.{total_results, results[], source}. $0.003 USDC on Base per call; 24h cached.

name: Greeneris Poland Company KYB
description: Polish company due-diligence (KYB) in one call: VAT status (Biala Lista, PL Ministry of Finance) plus KRS court-registry data — name, REGON, KRS, address, government-verified bank accounts (anti-fraud), legal form, capital, registration date and insolvency signals; looked up by NIP or KRS number.

krs.description: KRS court registry number, up to 10 digits

data.description: Company KYB record: nip, name, natural_person, vat_status, vat_active, regon, krs, address, vat_registration_date, bank_accounts[], bank_accounts_count, legal_form, capital{amount,currency}, registration_date, insolvency_signals[], source

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/pl/company?nip=<10-digit NIP>  OR  ?krs=<KRS number> (digits only; provide exactly one). Single x402 payment (Base USDC ~$0.003), no API key — payment is the auth. Result returned inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: { ok: true, data: { nip, name, natural_person, vat_status ('Czynny'=active), vat_active, regon, krs, address, vat_registration_date, bank_accounts[] (government-verified, anti-fraud), bank_accounts_count, legal_form, capital{amount,currency}, registration_date, insolvency_signals[] (KRS dzial 6: bankruptcy/restructuring/liquidation), source } }
quirks: Query by exactly one of ?nip= (10-digit Polish tax ID) or ?krs= (KRS court-registry number, up to 10 digits); digits only, no dashes or spaces.
Personal data (representatives, partners, clerks) is stripped for GDPR; sole-trader addresses are withheld.
bank_accounts[] are cross-checked against the government Biala Lista whitelist (anti-fraud); bank_accounts_count can be large (232 for ORLEN in the verified call).
Data combines Biala Lista VAT (wl-api.mf.gov.pl) and KRS (api-krs.ms.gov.pl); 24h cache.
Country-prefixed path — Poland only; sibling /v1/<cc>/company endpoints (fr, uk, ch, ie, cz, no, sk, fi) are distinct per-country services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Verify a Polish company / run KYB before invoicing or onboarding a PL partner. Call GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/pl/company with either ?nip=<10-digit tax ID> or ?krs=<court-registry number> (digits only). Pay once over x402 (Base USDC, ~$0.003, no API key). Read data: check vat_active/vat_status for VAT registration, insolvency_signals[] for bankruptcy/restructuring/liquidation flags, and bank_accounts[] (government-verified whitelist) to confirm a payment account before transferring funds.

name: Greeneris Slovak Company Lookup

q.description: Company name (3+ chars) or ICO, the 8-digit Slovak organisation id. Historic names also match; current-name hits rank first.

match_type.description: How the query was interpreted, e.g. 'ico' or 'name'

quirks: q is REQUIRED and accepts either a company name (3+ chars) or an 8-digit ICO (Slovak org id, e.g. 31333532); data.match_type reports how it was interpreted ('ico' vs 'name').
Name searches can be broad (q=eset returned total_results 269) — current-name hits rank first and historic names also match; use limit (1-5) to trim.

Static price ($0.003), not a dynamic quote; legal_form is a {code,name} pair in Slovak (e.g. 112 / 'Spolocnost s rucenim obmedzenym').
active_only defaults to false (includes terminated entities); set active_only=true to exclude them.
usage.guide: Look up a Slovak company in the official RPO business registry for KYB/due-diligence. Search by name: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/sk/company?q=eset&limit=1 (optional active_only=true) -> matches with ico/name/legal_form/status. Or fetch by ICO directly: GET .../v1/sk/company?q=31333532 -> the entity record (legal form, registered address, source register, established_on/terminated_on). Output: ok (bool) + data.{match_type, total_results, results[], source}. No API key — pay the x402 402 ($0.003 USDC on Base); 24h cached. For a French/Swiss/UK/etc. company use the sibling v1/fr|ch|uk|... /company endpoints instead.

name: Greeneris UK Company Registry
description: Official UK Companies House lookup by company name (?q=) or company number (?number=) — search returns matching companies (number, status, type, incorporation date); a number returns the full profile PLUS current officers and PSC (persons with significant control, the UK quasi-UBO register), risk flags (insolvency history, charges, overdue filings) and insolvency cases, for KYB and due diligence. Keyless over x402. $0.01.

q.description: Company name to search (returns matching companies). Use q OR number.

number.description: UK company number for the full profile + officers + PSC, e.g. 00445790. Use q OR number.

outputSchema.description: Profile mode (?number=): { ok, data: { company_number, name, status, company_type, jurisdiction, incorporated_on, ceased_on, sic_codes[], registered_office{ address_line_1, locality, postal_code, country }, risk_flags{ has_insolvency_history, has_charges, registered_office_in_dispute, accounts_overdue, confirmation_statement_overdue }, officers{ active_count, resigned_count, items[]{ name, role, appointed_on } }, psc{ total, items[] }, source } }. Search mode (?q=): matching companies with number, status, type, incorporation date.

usage.callShape: GET /v1/uk/company?number=<UK company number> for the full profile, OR GET /v1/uk/company?q=<company name>[&limit=1-10] to search
usage.outputShape: JSON. Profile (?number=): { ok:true, data:{ company_number, name, status, company_type, jurisdiction, incorporated_on, ceased_on, sic_codes[], registered_office{ address_line_1, locality, postal_code, country }, risk_flags{ has_insolvency_history, has_charges, registered_office_in_dispute, accounts_overdue, confirmation_statement_overdue }, officers{ active_count, resigned_count, items[]{ name, role, appointed_on } }, psc{ total, items[] }, source } }. Search (?q=): matching companies with number, status, type, incorporation date.
quirks: Two modes: ?q=<name> searches (list of matches); ?number=<UK company number> returns the FULL profile plus current officers and PSC. Provide exactly one of q or number.
PSC = persons with significant control (the UK quasi-UBO register): names, roles, natures of control; may be empty (total:0) when a company files PSC statements on Companies House instead.
risk_flags surface insolvency history, outstanding charges, and overdue filings for quick due-diligence triage; typed insolvency cases are included only when a history exists.
Officer/PSC data is minimized for privacy (no date of birth, no personal addresses) — statutory register data only.
Source is Companies House (api.company-information.service.gov.uk); responses are 24h cached.
For a French / Swiss / Czech / Polish / etc. company use the sibling v1/fr|ch|cz|pl|... /company endpoints instead — each is a distinct national registry.
usage.guide: UK KYB registry lookup over x402 (keyless, $0.01 on Base). To resolve a company from a name, GET ?q=<name> and read the matches; to pull a full dossier pass ?number=<UK company number> and read data.{registered_office, sic_codes, risk_flags, officers.items[], psc.items[]}. Use risk_flags (has_insolvency_history, has_charges, accounts_overdue, confirmation_statement_overdue) for a fast due-diligence verdict and psc.items[] for beneficial-ownership. Pay the 402 (Base USDC). For companies outside the UK use the sibling per-country /company endpoints.

name: OpenWebNinja Estimated Salary
description: Estimate the salary for a given job title in a given location, returning min/max/median total pay with base-salary and additional-pay (bonus/stock) breakdowns, salary period and currency, sample count, publisher and confidence — sourced from the JSearch (Google-for-Jobs) aggregate.

job_title.description: Job title to estimate the salary for, e.g. 'nodejs developer'. Required.

location.description: Location the estimate applies to, e.g. 'new york'. Free-text city/state/country. Required.

location_type.description: How to interpret the location string when matching salary data.

years_of_experience.description: Filter the estimate to a years-of-experience band.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include (field projection). All fields by default.

items.description: location, job_title, min_salary, max_salary, median_salary, min_base_salary, max_base_salary, median_base_salary, min_additional_pay, max_additional_pay, median_additional_pay, salary_period (HOUR|DAY|WEEK|MONTH|YEAR), salary_currency (ISO 4217), salary_count, salaries_updated_at (ISO 8601), publisher_name (e.g. Glassdoor), publisher_link, confidence (CONFIDENT|NOT_CONFIDENT).

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/jsearch/estimated-salary?job_title=<title>&location=<place>&location_type=ANY&years_of_experience=ALL — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum). The estimate is returned inline in the 200 JSON under data[]; no polling.
usage.outputShape: { status:'OK', request_id, parameters:{job_title,location,location_type,years_of_experience}, data:[ { location, job_title, min_salary, max_salary, median_salary, min_base_salary, max_base_salary, median_base_salary, min_additional_pay, max_additional_pay, median_additional_pay, salary_period, salary_currency, salary_count, salaries_updated_at, publisher_name, publisher_link, confidence } ] }. Verified with job_title='nodejs developer', location='new york' → HTTP 200, one entry: New York, NY, median total $153,861.42 (base $125,302.01 + additional $28,559.41), YEAR/USD, salary_count 6, publisher Glassdoor, confidence CONFIDENT.
quirks: job_title and location are the only required params; both are free text.

location_type (ANY|CITY|STATE|COUNTRY, default ANY) controls how the location string is matched; years_of_experience (ALL|LESS_THAN_ONE|ONE_TO_THREE|FOUR_TO_SIX|SEVEN_TO_NINE|TEN_TO_FOURTEEN|ABOVE_FIFTEEN, default ALL) narrows to an experience band.
