name: 2s NAICS Lookup
description: Look up or search NAICS 2022 US industry classification codes (US Census Bureau, public domain): pass an exact code for its official title, hierarchy path, description, activity-index terms and child codes, or a free-text industry description for ranked candidate codes.

code.description: Exact NAICS code (2-6 digits, or a combined sector range like 31-33). XOR with query.

query.description: Free-text industry or activity description to search. XOR with code.

level.description: Search mode only: restrict results to one hierarchy level (2=sector ... 6=national industry).

limit.description: Search mode only: max results, 1-50, default 20.

code.description: NAICS 2022 code (sectors may be ranges like 31-33).

heading.description: Ancestor path (sector > subsector > ...), excludes the code itself.

description.description: Official Census description. Full text on the exactly-matched code; truncated elsewhere.

indexTerms.description: Official activity index entries cross-referenced to this code.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/business/naics?query={text}&limit={1-50} OR ?code={naicsCode} (x402 paid, no request body). Provide EXACTLY ONE of code (exact-code lookup) or query (free-text search) - they are XOR. level (2-6) and limit (1-50) apply only in search mode.
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] (array). Each item: .code (NAICS 2022 code), .level (2-6), .title, .heading (ancestor path), .description (full text on the exactly-matched code, truncated/'See industry description for X' on others, sometimes 'NULL'), .indexTerms[] (nullable). body.data.ok, body.data.total, body.data.page{number,size,pages}, body.data.source{provider,url,license}. Settlement/cost echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: code and query are XOR - pass exactly one. code = exact-code lookup (returns the matched code first, then its direct children); query = free-text ranked search.
All inputs are query-string params, not path segments or a request body.

In exact-code lookup, full Census description text appears only on the exactly-matched code; child/parent items return truncated text, a 'See industry description for X' pointer, or the literal string 'NULL'.
level and limit are honored in search mode only (ignored for exact-code lookup); default limit is 20.
Results are paginated - body.data.page{number,size,pages} reports the page window; raise limit to fetch more candidates in one call.
Data is NAICS 2022 (US Census Bureau), public domain - US industry codes only.
Provider offers a free trial: append ?trial=1 for one free real call per endpoint per hour (not used for the registry price).
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/business/naics with EXACTLY ONE of two query params: query=<free-text industry description> (e.g. ?query=software+publishers) for a ranked search, or code=<NAICS code> (e.g. ?code=513210 or ?code=31-33) for an exact-code lookup. In search mode you may also pass level=2..6 to restrict to a hierarchy level and limit=1..50 (default 20). It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.001 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup - the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read matches from body.data.items[], each with .code, .level (2=sector ... 6=national industry), .title, .heading (ancestor path), .description (full official Census text on the exactly-matched code), and .indexTerms[]. Source is NAICS 2022 from the US Census Bureau (public domain); ground truth for industry coding in KYC/KYB, business registration, government filings, and ERP vendor/customer setup.

name: 2s Census Demographics
description: US Census ACS 5-year demographics for a state or county — pass a state (2-letter code or 2-digit FIPS) and optional 3-digit county FIPS to get population, median age, median household income, per-capita income, poverty rate, households, owner-occupancy rate, median home value, and median gross rent (US Census Bureau, public domain).

state.description: 2-letter state code or 2-digit FIPS (required). e.g. 'TX' or '48'.

county.description: 3-digit county FIPS (omit for state-level). e.g. '201' = Harris County, TX.

year.description: ACS data year (default latest available; latest observed = 2023).

backends.outputSchema: { data: { ok: boolean, items[]: { query:{state,county,year}, geoName (string, e.g. 'Harris County, Texas'), population (int), medianAge (number), medianHouseholdIncomeUSD (int), perCapitaIncomeUSD (int), povertyRate (number 0..1, computed), households (int), ownerOccupancyRate (number 0..1, computed), medianHomeValueUSD (int), medianGrossRentUSD (int), source:{provider,url,license}, note (methodology; nulls where Census suppresses) }, total (int), source:{provider,url,license} }, meta: { endpoint:'census.demographics', version, caller, cost:{usd}, settlement:{txHash,network,success} } }

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/census/demographics?state={2-letter or 2-digit FIPS}&county={3-digit FIPS}&year={YYYY} — state required; county optional (omit for state-level); year optional (default latest). All query-string params, no request body.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Result under body.data.items[] (array, usually one geography). items[0]: {query{state,county,year}, geoName, population, medianAge, medianHouseholdIncomeUSD, perCapitaIncomeUSD, povertyRate (0..1, computed), households, ownerOccupancyRate (0..1, computed), medianHomeValueUSD, medianGrossRentUSD, source{provider,url,license}, note}. body.data.total (count), body.data.source{provider,url,license}. Cost at body.meta.cost.usd; settlement at body.meta.settlement{txHash,network,success}.
quirks: Result is nested under body.data.items[] (an array even for a single geography) — read items[0].
state, county and year are query-string params, not path segments or a JSON body.
state is required (2-letter code like 'TX' OR 2-digit FIPS like '48'); county is a 3-digit FIPS (e.g. '201' = Harris County, TX) — omit county for state-level totals.
povertyRate and ownerOccupancyRate are decimals in 0..1 (computed by the provider: poverty = below-poverty / universe; owner-occupancy = owner / occupied units), NOT percentages.
Fields can be null where the Census Bureau suppresses or has no estimate; see items[0].note for methodology.
Data is US Census Bureau ACS 5-Year (latest observed year 2023), public domain — US geographies only. Complements a ZIP/ZCTA-level census endpoint with state/county geography.
Provider offers a free trial on 2s.io endpoints (?trial=1, one free real call per endpoint per hour) — not used for the registry price.
usage.guide: Fetch authoritative US Census ACS 5-year demographics for a state or county. Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/census/demographics with query param state (required — a 2-letter code like 'TX' or a 2-digit FIPS like '48') and optionally county (a 3-digit county FIPS, e.g. '201' = Harris County; omit for state-level totals) and year (defaults to the latest ACS year, 2023). No request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.00108 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON — read the result from body.data.items[0]: geoName, population, medianAge, medianHouseholdIncomeUSD, perCapitaIncomeUSD, povertyRate (decimal 0..1), households, ownerOccupancyRate (decimal 0..1), medianHomeValueUSD, medianGrossRentUSD. Some fields may be null where the Census suppresses an estimate. Source is US Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year, public domain — use for market sizing, site selection, and socioeconomic research (data an LLM cannot reliably recall). Verified 2026-07-30 with {state:'TX',county:'201'} -> HTTP 200 (Harris County, Texas: population 4,758,579, medianHouseholdIncomeUSD 73,104), $0.00108 charged (tx 0xa214fce78a36a219b474ddc42781628a8770c8046b5c18bd491921adb6787030).

name: 2s FDA Food Recalls
description: Search FDA food recall enforcement reports (OpenFDA /food/enforcement), newest first by report date — filter by product keyword, recall classification (Class I/II/III), status (Ongoing/Completed/Terminated/Pending), or US state; each record has recall number, product description, reason for recall, recalling firm + location, distribution pattern, and recall/report dates.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params (all optional; a plain limit-only call returns the most recent recalls): product (string, product-description keyword), classification (string, one of 'I','II','III' or 'Class I'/'Class II'/'Class III'), status (string, one of 'Ongoing','Completed','Terminated','Pending'), state (string, 2-letter US state code), limit (integer, default 20). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { data: { ok: boolean, items[]: { recallNumber (string), status (string), classification (string, 'Class I'|'Class II'|'Class III'), productType (string, 'Food'), productDescription (string), reasonForRecall (string), initialNotification (string), voluntaryMandated (string), recallingFirm (string), city (string), state (string), country (string), distributionPattern (string), recallInitiationDate (string YYYY-MM-DD), reportDate (string YYYY-MM-DD) }, total (int), source: {provider,url,license}, meta: { query:{product,classification,status,state,limit} } }, meta: { endpoint, version, caller, cost:{usd}, settlement:{txHash,network,success} } }

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/gov/fda-food-recalls?status={Ongoing|Completed|Terminated|Pending}&classification={I|II|III}&product={keyword}&state={XX}&limit={n} — all query params optional; a limit-only call returns the most recent recalls. No request body.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Recall rows under body.data.items[] (array), each: {recallNumber, status, classification ('Class I'|'Class II'|'Class III'), productType, productDescription, reasonForRecall, initialNotification, voluntaryMandated, recallingFirm, city, state, country, distributionPattern, recallInitiationDate (YYYY-MM-DD), reportDate (YYYY-MM-DD)}. body.data.total (total matching count, 1067 for status=Ongoing at index time), body.data.source {provider='OpenFDA — Food Recall Enforcement Reports', url, license='Public domain (US government records)'}, body.data.meta.query (echoed filters). Cost at body.meta.cost.usd; settlement at body.meta.settlement {txHash,network,success}.
quirks: Results are nested under body.data.items[] (an array) — read items[], not the top level.
All parameters are query-string params, not path segments or a JSON body.

classification accepts the roman-numeral filter 'I'/'II'/'III' (or the full 'Class I' etc.); response rows return the full form e.g. 'Class I'. Class I = most serious (reasonable probability of serious health consequences), Class III = least.
status enum: Ongoing / Completed / Terminated / Pending — pass exactly (title-case); results are ordered newest-first by reportDate.
state is a 2-letter US state code and filters on the recalling-firm / distribution location; foreign firms may have an empty state and a non-US country (e.g. Chile).

Data is backed by OpenFDA's /food/enforcement endpoint (US government records, public domain); body.data.total is the full match count — use limit to page (no explicit offset param observed in the live schema).
distributionPattern is free-text prose describing shipped states/countries, not a structured list.
usage.guide: Search FDA food recall enforcement reports (backed by OpenFDA's /food/enforcement dataset), newest first by report date. Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/gov/fda-food-recalls with any of these optional query params: limit (integer, default 20), status ('Ongoing'|'Completed'|'Terminated'|'Pending'), classification ('I'|'II'|'III', Class I = most serious), product (product-description keyword), state (2-letter US state code). A limit-only call returns the most recent recalls. No request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0024 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key. The response is synchronous JSON — read recall rows from body.data.items[] (each has recallNumber, status, classification, productDescription, reasonForRecall, recallingFirm, city/state/country, distributionPattern, recallInitiationDate, reportDate); body.data.total is the total match count and body.data.source gives provenance (OpenFDA, public domain). Verified 2026-07-30 with {limit:20,status:'Ongoing'} -> HTTP 200 (total 1067), $0.0024 charged (tx 0x3a156030e8e429331e376f630596b25a4c837822bebf26b1ed05033f094c04c2).

name: 2s OSHA Violations
description: Search OSHA citation / violation records (~13.2M citations) from the US Department of Labor Open Data Portal — filter by inspection activity number, citation id, 29 CFR standard, issuance-date range, initial-penalty range, or emphasis-program code, and pair with OSHA inspections to trace site to inspection to violation.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params (all optional; a plain limit-only call returns the most recent citations): activityNr (integer, OSHA inspection activity number), citationId (string), standard (string, 29 CFR standard e.g. '19100132'), issuanceDateMin (string YYYY-MM-DD), issuanceDateMax (string YYYY-MM-DD), initialPenalty (object {min,max} — nested object, encode the min/max sub-fields), emphasis (string, emphasis-program code), fields (string, comma-separated field projection), sort (string), limit (integer 1..100, default 25), offset (integer >=0, default 0). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { data: { ok: boolean, items[]: { activity_nr (int), citation_id (string), delete_flag, standard (string, 29 CFR), viol_type (S=serious etc.), issuance_date (ISO), abate_date, abate_complete, current_penalty (number|null), initial_penalty (number|null), contest_date, final_order_date, nr_instances (int), nr_exposed (int), rec, gravity, emphasis, hazcat, hazsub1..hazsub5, fta_* fields, load_dt (ISO) }, total (int, ~13.25M), source: {provider,url,license}, meta: {nextOffset} }, meta: { endpoint, version, caller, cost:{usd}, settlement:{txHash,network,success} } }

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/gov/osha-violations?limit={n}&standard={cfr}&initialPenalty.min={usd}&issuanceDateMin={YYYY-MM-DD}&activityNr={n} — all query params optional; a limit-only call returns the most recent citations. No request body.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Citation rows under body.data.items[] (array), each: {activity_nr, citation_id, standard (29 CFR), viol_type, issuance_date (ISO), abate_date, initial_penalty (number|null), current_penalty (number|null), nr_instances, nr_exposed, gravity, emphasis, hazsub1..5, load_dt, ...}. body.data.total (total matching count, ~13.25M), body.data.meta.nextOffset (paging cursor), body.data.source {provider,url,license=public domain}. Cost at body.meta.cost.usd; settlement at body.meta.settlement {txHash,network,success}.
quirks: Results are nested under body.data.items[] (an array) — read items[], not the top level.
All parameters are query-string params, not path segments or a JSON body.

The bazaar callHint suggested a 'state' param, but it is NOT in the live openapi/402 schema and is ignored; filter geographically via the linked /api/gov/osha-inspections join instead. Verified valid filters: activityNr, citationId, standard, issuanceDateMin/Max, initialPenalty{min,max}, emphasis, fields, sort, limit, offset.

initialPenalty is a nested object {min,max}; encoding it as flat query keys (e.g. initialPenalty.min=50000) may be ignored by the backend (the paid test with that key still returned unfiltered low-penalty rows). Prefer standard/date filters for reliable narrowing.

standard is a 29 CFR code without punctuation (e.g. '19100132' = PPE general requirements, '19100157' = portable fire extinguishers); the value may include a sub-part suffix like '19100036 B01' in results.
current_penalty and initial_penalty can be null; many historical rows omit penalty amounts.

Each citation links to an inspection via activity_nr — pair with /api/gov/osha-inspections to trace site -> inspection -> violation. Data source is US DoL Open Data Portal (v4), US Government work, public domain.
total (~13.25M) is the full corpus/match count; use limit (1..100) and offset / meta.nextOffset to page.
usage.guide: Search OSHA citation/violation records from the US Department of Labor Open Data Portal (~13.2M citations). Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/gov/osha-violations with any of these optional query params: limit (1..100, default 25), offset (>=0), standard (29 CFR code, e.g. '19100132' for PPE), issuanceDateMin / issuanceDateMax (YYYY-MM-DD), activityNr (OSHA inspection activity number), citationId, emphasis (program code), fields (projection), sort. A limit-only call returns the most recent citations. No request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0012 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key. The response is synchronous JSON — read citation rows from body.data.items[] (each has activity_nr, citation_id, standard, viol_type, issuance_date, initial_penalty, nr_exposed, etc.); body.data.total is the total match count and body.data.meta.nextOffset is the paging cursor. Each row's activity_nr joins to /api/gov/osha-inspections to trace establishment -> inspection -> violation. Note the callHint's 'state' param is not supported by the live schema and is ignored. Source is US DoL Open Data Portal (v4), public domain. Verified 2026-07-30 with {limit:3} -> HTTP 200, $0.0012 charged (tx 0xcea3369d1caa06e29c8ed20fa3cafd75eb106660c1135779ff00bf86a00d9154).

name: 2s CFR Section
description: Fetch the authoritative full text of any US Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) section by title and section number from the Electronic CFR (US GPO / Office of the Federal Register) — returns the canonical citation, section heading, full plain text, Federal Register source credit, as-of date, and official eCFR link, with optional point-in-time historical text back to 2017.

title.description: CFR title number, 1-50 (e.g. 12 for Banks and Banking, 40 for Protection of Environment). Required query param.

section.description: Section identifier as "part.section", e.g. "1026.43" or "240.10b-5" (the part is the digits before the dot). Must contain a dot. Required query param.

date.description: Optional point-in-time date (YYYY-MM-DD). Returns the text in force on that date; coverage starts 2017-01-03. Defaults to the latest available text.

truncated.description: True if text was cut at the response cap (rare, giant sections only).

url.description: Official eCFR page for the section.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/law/cfr-section?title={1-50}&section={part.section} (x402 paid, no request body). title (integer 1-50) and section (string "part.section" e.g. 1026.43, must contain a dot) are required query params; optional date (YYYY-MM-DD) returns historical text in force on that date (back to 2017-01-03).
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. The single CFR section is under body.data.items[0] (items is always a one-element array, body.data.total=1). Each item: .citation (e.g. "12 CFR 1026.43"), .title (int), .part, .section, .heading ("§ 1026.43 Minimum standards ..."), .text (full plain-text body of the section), .sourceCredit (Federal Register citation history, nullable), .asOfDate (yyyy-mm-dd the text reflects), .truncated (bool, true only for rare giant sections cut at the response cap), .url (official eCFR page). body.data.ok, body.data.source{provider,url,license=Public domain}. Cost/settlement echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: The result is nested under body.data.items[] (always a single-element array for a valid title+section) — read items[0], not a top-level items.
title and section are query-string params, not path segments or a JSON body.

section MUST be the "part.section" form containing a dot (e.g. "1026.43", "240.10b-5"); a bare number like "1" fails the section pattern and would buy a paid HTTP 400. The bazaar/callHint example value (section:"1") is invalid — use the openapi documented form.
text can be very large (this example returned ~55KB of section body); .truncated flags the rare case where a giant section is cut at the response cap.
Optional date (YYYY-MM-DD) retrieves the historical text in force on that date; coverage starts 2017-01-03, defaults to latest.
US federal regulations only. Data is the Electronic CFR (US GPO / Office of the Federal Register), public domain, updated daily.
Provider offers a free trial: append ?trial=1 for one free real call per endpoint per hour (not used for the registry price).
usage.guide: Fetch the authoritative full text of a US Code of Federal Regulations section. Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/law/cfr-section with required query params title (integer 1-50, the CFR title — e.g. 12 for Banks and Banking, 40 for Protection of Environment) and section (string in "part.section" form containing a dot, e.g. "1026.43" or "240.10b-5"); optionally add date (YYYY-MM-DD) to get the historical text in force on that date (back to 2017). No request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0018 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read the section from body.data.items[0] — .citation, .heading, the full .text, .sourceCredit, .asOfDate, and .url (official eCFR page). Data is the Electronic CFR (US GPO / Office of the Federal Register), public domain, updated daily — use it to verify regulatory citations against the authoritative source. Note: section must contain a dot; a bare number fails validation. Verified 2026-07-31 with {title:12, section:'1026.43'} → HTTP 200, $0.0018 charged (tx 0x63d250ec6b3580a02d0ef90943efe883ac9ca133214ff314dc92dc20b0fbdc6e), returned the full text of Regulation Z §1026.43.

name: 2s Docket Search
description: Search US federal court dockets — civil and criminal — from the CourtListener / RECAP-PACER archive by case name or party (full-text q), optional court, filed-date range, or exact docket number, returning each matched docket's id, case name, court, docket number, dates filed/terminated, nature of suit, assigned judge, and public docket URL.

q.description: Free-text search over case name / party, e.g. "United States v. Bankman-Fried".

court.description: Optional CourtListener court id to scope results, e.g. "cand", "nysd", "ca9".

docketNumber.description: Exact docket number for direct lookup, e.g. "1:22-cr-00673" (pair with court).

filedAfter.description: Only dockets filed on/after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

filedBefore.description: Only dockets filed on/before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

court.description: Human-readable court name, e.g. "District Court, S.D. New York".

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/law/docket-search?q={case name or party} (x402 paid, no request body). All params are query-string and optional, but supply at least one selector: q (free-text case/party, 2-300 chars) OR docketNumber (+ court) for exact lookup. Optional court (CourtListener court id like "nysd", "cand", "ca9"), filedAfter/filedBefore (YYYY-MM-DD), page (1-based).
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Matched dockets are under body.data.items[] (an array). Each item: .docketId (number), .caseName, .court (human name), .courtId (CourtListener id), .docketNumber, .dateFiled, .dateTerminated (nullable), .natureOfSuit (nullable), .assignedTo (judge), .url (public CourtListener docket page). body.data.total is the upstream match count (e.g. 733 for the example; the page returns up to ~20 items — paginate with page). body.data.ok, body.data.source{provider="CourtListener / RECAP archive", url, license="Public court records via Free Law Project (CC0)"}. Cost/settlement echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: Results are nested under body.data.items[] (not a top-level items) and body.data.total holds the full upstream match count while items is one page (~20) — use the page param to page through.
All params are query-string and technically optional; you must pass at least one selector (q, or docketNumber). q is full-text over case name/party.

The same case often appears as multiple docket rows (different courts/appeals/JPML entries, and CourtListener sometimes has several archived snapshots of one docket number) — dedupe on docketNumber+courtId if you need unique cases.
court/courtId use CourtListener court ids (e.g. "nysd", "cand", "ca9", "jpml", "deb"), not full names.
US federal courts only. Data is the CourtListener / RECAP-PACER archive (Free Law Project, CC0 public records).
Sibling endpoints on the same host: /api/law/case-search (opinions full-text) and /api/law/opinion (full opinion text).
Provider offers a free trial: append ?trial=1 for one free real call per endpoint per hour (not used for the registry price).
usage.guide: Search US federal court dockets (civil and criminal) from the CourtListener / RECAP-PACER archive. Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/law/docket-search with a query param q for a free-text case-name/party search (e.g. q="United States v. Bankman-Fried"), or docketNumber (+ court) for an exact lookup; optionally scope with court (a CourtListener court id like "nysd", "cand", "ca9"), filedAfter/filedBefore (YYYY-MM-DD), and page (1-based). No request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0048 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read matched dockets from body.data.items[] (each has caseName, court/courtId, docketNumber, dateFiled/dateTerminated, natureOfSuit, assignedTo judge, and a public .url), with body.data.total giving the full match count (paginate via page). Data is public court records (Free Law Project, CC0). Useful for litigation monitoring, criminal-case research, and KYC/due-diligence. Verified 2026-07-30 with {q:'United States v. Bankman-Fried'} → HTTP 200, $0.0048 charged (tx 0x9896f5d7cb0f4891d9685eeafe3ffa5a430d7649d6b3e8f22f60dd89271b3f68), returned 733 total matches including the SDNY criminal case 1:22-cr-00673 before Judge Lewis A. Kaplan.

name: 2s Trademark Search
description: Full-text search of the US trademark register (USPTO) by wordmark text, owner name, or goods/services — returning each mark's serial, registration number, status, dates, owner, and Nice classes. Pay-per-call x402.

inputSchema.description: Provide `query` for full-text search, OR `serial`/`registrationNumber` for an exact record.

query.description: Free-text search over wordmark (default), owner, or goods/services.

serial.description: Exact USPTO serial number (digits) for a single record.

registrationNumber.description: Exact USPTO registration number for a single record.

field.description: Which text to search. Default mark.

intlClass.description: Nice international class filter, e.g. 9 or 009.

outputSchema.description: Wrapped response: results live under data.items[]; billing/settlement under meta.

total.description: Total matches for the query across all pages.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/law/trademark-search?query={query}&status={status} (x402 paid, no request body). Use query for full-text search, OR serial/registrationNumber for an exact record; optional filters field (mark|owner|all), status (live|all), intlClass, limit, offset.
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] is the array of matching trademarks; each item has markText, serialNumber, registrationNumber ('0000000' if not yet registered), status{code,label,date,live}, filingDate, registrationDate, abandonmentDate, cancellationDate, renewalDate, owner, intlClasses[] (Nice classes), goodsServices, markDrawingCode. body.data.total = total matches across all pages; body.data.page{number,size,pages} for pagination. body.data.source names the corpus (USPTO Trademark Full-Text Bulk Data, public domain). body.meta.cost.usd + body.meta.settlement.txHash confirm payment.
quirks: Response is double-wrapped: read marks from body.data.items[] (NOT top-level items), matching other 2s.io endpoints.
Only 20 items are returned per call by default (limit max 100); body.data.total can be large (the 'apple' example reported total=1509 across 76 pages) — page with limit/offset.
registrationNumber is '0000000' for marks still pending (not yet registered); use status.live and status.label to interpret prosecution state.
status=live (default) returns registered+pending only; pass status=all to include dead/abandoned marks.

Corpus is the USPTO full trademark register (public-domain bulk data), refreshed periodically — not the live real-time USPTO TSDR feed; the provider suggests law.trademark-status for live prosecution detail on a known serial.
usage.guide: Search the US trademark register. Send a GET to https://2s.io/api/law/trademark-search with either query (free-text over wordmark by default, or owner/goods when field=owner|all) OR serial / registrationNumber for an exact record. Optional filters: field (mark|owner|all), status (live default = registered+pending; all = includes dead/abandoned), intlClass (Nice class e.g. 9), limit (1-100, default 20), offset (pagination). No request body. The x402 payment ($0.0024 USDC on Base or Solana) is handled by the pay layer. On success (200) read body.data.items[] — each match has markText, serialNumber, registrationNumber, status{code,label,date,live}, filing/registration/abandonment/renewal dates, owner, intlClasses[], and goodsServices; body.data.total gives the full match count for pagination. Data is USPTO Trademark Full-Text Bulk Data (US public domain). Verified 2026-07-31 with {query:'apple', status:'live'} -> HTTP 200, total 1509, $0.0024 charged (tx 0xdd10c613b1f942b1d52175708359211c0790b7757a57f43e7a5d86a46d931f9d).

name: 2s US Code Section
description: Fetch the authoritative current text of any United States Code section by title (1-54) and section number, returning the canonical citation, heading, hierarchy context, full statutory plain text, Statutes-at-Large source credit, and the official OLRC link.

title.description: USC title number, 1-54 (e.g. 17 for Copyrights, 26 for Internal Revenue Code, 42 for Public Health and Welfare).

section.description: Section number, e.g. "107", "78j", or "1395w-4" (hyphenated/lettered sections work).

includeNotes.description: Include editorial notes (amendment history, effective dates, cross-references). Default false — notes can be long.

truncated.description: True if a block was cut at the response cap (rare).

url.description: Official uscode.house.gov page for the section.

total.description: Total matching rows upstream; null when unknown.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/law/usc-section?title={1-54}&section={string} (x402 paid, no request body). Both title and section are required query-string params. Optional includeNotes=true adds editorial notes.
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] (array, usually one item). Each item: .citation (e.g. '17 U.S.C. § 107'), .title, .section, .heading, .context (hierarchy breadcrumb), .text (full statutory plain text), .sourceCredit (Statutes-at-Large cite), .notes (only when includeNotes=true, else null), .truncated, .edition ('prelim' = current law), .url (official OLRC page). Also body.data.ok, body.data.total, body.data.source{provider,url,license}. Settlement/cost echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: Both title and section are REQUIRED query-string params (not path segments, not a request body).
title is 1-54; section is a string so hyphenated/lettered sections like '78j' or '1395w-4' work.
includeNotes defaults to false — editorial notes (amendment history, effective dates) can be very long; set includeNotes=true to include them.
Serves the OLRC current 'prelim' edition (public domain, US government work) — authoritative for verifying statutory citations rather than relying on model memory.
Different endpoint from siblings: /api/law/cfr-section is the Code of Federal REGULATIONS (not the US Code), and /api/law/case-verify is case law.
Provider offers a free trial on 2s endpoints (append ?trial=1) — not used for the registry price.
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/law/usc-section with two required query params: title=<1-54> and section=<string> (e.g. ?title=17&section=107 for the fair-use statute). Optionally add includeNotes=true to also return editorial notes (amendment history, effective dates). It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0018 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read the statute from body.data.items[0], which carries .citation, .heading, .context (title/chapter breadcrumb), .text (full statutory plain text), .sourceCredit (Statutes-at-Large enactment/amendment cites), .edition ('prelim' = current law), and .url (the official uscode.house.gov page). Source is the Office of the Law Revision Counsel, US House of Representatives (public domain) — authoritative ground truth for statutory text in legal research, compliance, and citation verification. For federal regulations use /api/law/cfr-section; for case law use /api/law/case-verify.

name: 2s Person Cross-Registry
description: Sweep a person's full name across five independent US public registries in one call — FINRA BrokerCheck securities brokers, federal-court attorneys (CourtListener), federal inmates (Bureau of Prisons), Texas trade licenses (TDLR), and Texas real-estate licenses (TREC). Returns one block per registry with found/error status, match count, and the matching records as name-matched CANDIDATES (deliberately not merged into one identity — same name does not mean same person). A due-diligence, KYC-screening-triage, and background-research staple; each registry is also a standalone endpoint for follow-up by identifier (CRD, license number, inmate number).

name.description: Person full name, e.g. "John Smith". Partial matching per registry.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/person/cross-registry?name={full name}&limit={1-10} — inputs are URL query params, no request body. name is required; limit (max matches per registry, default 5) is optional. Pay $0.0072 USDC via x402 (Base or Solana); result returned synchronously in the 200 JSON body.
usage.outputShape: Sync JSON under body.data: .name (echoed query), .note (identity-resolution caveat), and five per-registry blocks each shaped {found:boolean, error:null|string, count:integer, matches:[]}: .brokers (FINRA — matches have crd, firstName/middleName/lastName, otherNames[], bcScope/iaScope, hasDisclosures, finraRegistrationCount, currentEmployments[]{firmId,firmName,branchCity,branchState}), .attorneys (CourtListener — id, name, firm, caseCount, url, dateModified), .inmates (BOP — name{first,middle,last,suffix}, inmateNumber, sex, race, age, facility{code,name,type}, projected/actualReleaseDate, releaseCode), .txTrades (TDLR — licenseType, licenseNumber, ownerName), .txRealEstate (TREC — licenseType, licenseNumber, name, status, originalLicenseDate, expires, supervisor). Plus body.data.sources[] {provider,url,license} provenance for all five. Top-level body.meta has endpoint (person.cross-registry), cost.usd, settlement{txHash,network,success}.
quirks: Inputs are URL query params on a GET (no request body). Only name is required; limit (1-10, default 5) caps matches PER registry, not overall.
Result payload is nested under body.data (not top-level); each registry is its own object with independent found/error/count/matches[].

Matches are name-matched CANDIDATES, deliberately NOT identity-resolved — the same name in two registries does not mean the same person. Verify with each registry's own identifier (CRD, attorney id, inmate number, license number) before acting.
Registry coverage is partly TEXAS-scoped: txTrades (TDLR) and txRealEstate (TREC) are Texas-only; brokers (FINRA), attorneys (CourtListener federal courts), and inmates (federal BOP) are national.
A per-registry block can independently fail — check block.error / block.found rather than assuming all five succeeded.

Each registry is also a standalone endpoint (/api/license/broker, /api/law/attorney-lookup, /api/gov/inmate-locator, /api/license/trades, /api/license/real-estate) for follow-up lookups by identifier.

Data licenses are all public-records: FINRA BrokerCheck terms, CourtListener/Free Law Project public-domain court records, US-government-work BOP data, and Texas Public Information Act (data.texas.gov).
Advertises two accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) and Solana USDC; paid cleanly on Base at $0.0072.
usage.guide: Screen a person's name against five US public registries at once. GET https://2s.io/api/person/cross-registry?name=<full name> (optional &limit=1..10 to cap matches per registry, default 5). No request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0072 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON under body.data with five per-registry blocks — brokers (FINRA BrokerCheck), attorneys (CourtListener federal courts), inmates (federal Bureau of Prisons), txTrades (Texas TDLR trade licenses), txRealEstate (Texas TREC real-estate licenses) — each {found,error,count,matches[]}, plus body.data.sources[] provenance. Treat matches as name-matched CANDIDATES only: verify with each registry's identifier (CRD, attorney id, inmate number, license number) before acting, and follow up via the per-registry standalone endpoints. Note txTrades/txRealEstate are Texas-only. Use for due-diligence, KYC-screening triage, and background research. Verified 2026-07-31 with {name:'John Smith',limit:3} -> HTTP 200 (3 brokers incl. CRD 6808119 @ Vanguard, 3 attorneys, 3 BOP inmates, 0 TX trades, 2 TX real-estate agents), $0.0072 charged (tx 0xbaf3ab3d188e813f8195a8c79c68f73211344f28debe4a7dc940de4a5a967d74).

name: Agentstools Device Adverse Events
description: FDA MAUDE adverse-event summary for a medical-device brand or generic device name — total report count plus deaths, injuries and malfunctions broken down by event type, sourced from openFDA, for device-safety monitoring and clinical-risk agents. Informational, not medical advice. Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params. Required: brand (string — medical-device brand or generic device name, e.g. 'pacemaker', 'insulin pump'). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { query: {brand (string — echoed)}, found (bool — whether any MAUDE reports matched), device_events: {brand (string), total_reports (int), deaths (int), injuries (int), malfunctions (int), by_event_type (object mapping event-type name e.g. 'Malfunction'|'Injury'|'Death' -> count)}, sources: {partial (bool), providers[] (e.g. ['device_event']), errors? (object mapping provider -> upstream error string when partial)}, attribution[] (openFDA/FDA attribution notice), disclaimer (string — informational, not medical advice) }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/device/adverse-events?brand=<device brand or generic name> — single required query param `brand`, no request body. x402 paid endpoint, $0.02 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. device_events holds the aggregate MAUDE counts for the brand — total_reports plus deaths, injuries and malfunctions, and by_event_type mapping each FDA event-type label to its count. found signals whether any reports matched. sources.partial=true (with sources.errors) indicates one or more upstream openFDA queries failed for this call. attribution[] and disclaimer carry the openFDA licensing/medical-disclaimer notes. Example (from the provider, brand='pacemaker'): total_reports 33709, deaths 804, injuries 7856, malfunctions 24899.
quirks: Only `brand` is required and it is a query param — there is no request body.

Data is the FDA MAUDE (Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience) DEVICE adverse-event database via openFDA — distinct from FAERS drug adverse events (see the separate /drug/adverse-events endpoint).
Informational aggregation of public FDA data — NOT medical advice, NOT a diagnosis; openFDA data does not imply FDA endorsement (see the response disclaimer/attribution).

The endpoint fans out to upstream openFDA (open.fda.gov); if that upstream is throttled it returns HTTP 200 with sources.partial=true, sources.errors and zeroed counts rather than a hard error — retry to get populated counts.
found=false with all-zero counts means either no matching MAUDE reports OR a partial upstream failure — check sources.partial/errors to tell them apart.
Price $0.02 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key. The x402 quote lives in the base64 'payment-required' response header, not the JSON body (body is empty {}).
usage.guide: Look up FDA MAUDE medical-device adverse-event counts for a device brand or generic name — a cheap safety-signal check for device-risk, procurement-diligence or clinical agents. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/device/adverse-events with the single required `brand` query param (a medical-device brand or generic device name, e.g. 'pacemaker' or 'insulin pump'); no request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.02 USDC on Base; no API key, synchronous, no polling. Read device_events for the aggregate counts — total_reports plus deaths, injuries, malfunctions, and by_event_type (a map of each FDA event-type label to its count); found tells you whether any reports matched. Data comes from the FDA MAUDE device database via openFDA (distinct from FAERS drug adverse events at /drug/adverse-events). Check sources.partial/sources.errors: the endpoint fans out to upstream open.fda.gov and, if that upstream is throttled, returns a 200 with partial=true and zeroed counts (retry to get real numbers). Informational only, not medical advice (see the response disclaimer/attribution). Verified 2026-07-31 with {brand:'insulin pump'} -> HTTP 200 in the documented shape, $0.02 charged on Base (on that call upstream openFDA returned a transient 403 so counts came back partial/zero; the provider's own example for brand='pacemaker' shows total_reports 33709 / deaths 804 / injuries 7856 / malfunctions 24899).

name: Agentstools Drug Adverse Events
description: Aggregate FDA FAERS adverse-event summary for a drug (via openFDA) by brand, generic or active-ingredient name — top reported reactions with counts, the serious and death-flagged fractions, and a demographic breakdown as aggregate counts. Informational, not medical advice. Keyless pay-per-call x402.

drug.description: Drug brand, generic or active-ingredient name to look up FAERS adverse-event reports for (e.g. "ibuprofen"). Passed as a query-string parameter, not a body.
Echo of the requested drug name.

found.description: Whether adverse-event data was retrieved for the drug (false when the upstream openFDA fetch fails or no reports match).

adverse_events.description: Aggregate FAERS summary (populated only when found=true; empty {} otherwise).

total_reports.description: Total number of FAERS reports for the drug.

death_fraction.description: Fraction (0-1) of reports flagged as death outcomes.

partial.description: True when one or more upstream providers failed and the result is incomplete.

errors.description: Per-provider error messages (present only on failure), e.g. {drug_event: "upstream api.fda.gov returned HTTP 403"}.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/adverse-events?drug={drug name} — the `drug` query-string param is REQUIRED (brand, generic or active-ingredient name); no request body. Result is returned inline in the 200 (synchronous). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON: query{drug} (echo), found (boolean), adverse_events{} (aggregate FAERS summary — populated only when found=true: total_reports (int), serious_fraction (0-1), death_fraction (0-1), top_reactions[] each {reaction (MedDRA term), count} — plus a demographic breakdown as aggregate counts per the 402 description), sources{partial (bool), errors{} (per-provider failures), providers[]}, attribution[] (openFDA public-data notice), disclaimer (not-medical-advice). NOTE: on the paid verification call the upstream api.fda.gov/openFDA returned a transient HTTP 403 so this response came back found:false, adverse_events:{}, sources:{errors:{drug_event:"upstream api.fda.gov returned HTTP 403"}, partial:true, providers:["drug_event"]} — the endpoint, payment path and envelope are verified live; the adverse_events data fields are from the provider's documented 402 output example (total_reports 90000, serious_fraction 0.6, death_fraction 0.04, top_reactions[{reaction:'NAUSEA',count:4200}]) and were NOT populated on this particular call.
quirks: `drug` is a REQUIRED query-string parameter (brand, generic or active-ingredient name); there is no request body and no other params. The 402 schema lists methods GET/HEAD/DELETE but GET is the documented working call.

TRANSIENT UPSTREAM 403: the paid verification call returned HTTP 200 but found:false / adverse_events:{} because upstream api.fda.gov (openFDA) returned a 403 (sources.errors.drug_event='upstream api.fda.gov returned HTTP 403', partial:true). openFDA rate-limits/blocks by IP; retry later or from a different egress to get populated data. The charge still applies on an empty result.
Always inspect `found` and `sources.partial` before reading `adverse_events` — the object is empty {} when the upstream fetch fails or nothing matches.

Data is FDA FAERS via openFDA (open.fda.gov), public domain; the response carries an attribution[] string and a disclaimer that must be preserved when displaying results. Informational aggregation only — NOT medical advice, diagnosis or a guarantee.

402 advertises Base USDC only ($0.02, amount 20000, 6-decimal); no Solana leg on this endpoint. The x402 quote (accepts) lives in the base64 `payment-required` response header — the JSON body is empty {}.

Same public FAERS/openFDA source as the Stratalize FAERS proposals but a distinct provider/host/price/shape (cheaper, no attestation receipts, `drug` vs `drug_name` input) — kept as its own service, not a backend.
usage.guide: Get an aggregate FDA drug-safety (adverse-event) summary for any drug with one keyless x402 call. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/adverse-events with the REQUIRED `drug` query param (brand, generic or active-ingredient name, e.g. drug=ibuprofen); no request body, no API key — the ~$0.02 USDC payment on Base is handled by the pay layer. Synchronous: read the 200 JSON directly. FIRST check `found` and `sources.partial`: when found=true, `adverse_events` gives total_reports, serious_fraction and death_fraction (0-1) and top_reactions[] (MedDRA term + count), plus a demographic breakdown as aggregate counts; when found=false the upstream openFDA fetch failed (see sources.errors, e.g. a transient api.fda.gov 403) and adverse_events is empty {} — retry later. Preserve the attribution[] and disclaimer (openFDA public data; informational only, NOT medical advice). Verified 2026-07-31 with {drug:'ibuprofen'} -> HTTP 200, $0.02 charged on Base; on that call openFDA returned a transient 403 so adverse_events came back empty (endpoint/payment/envelope confirmed; data example values above are from the provider's own 402 documentation).

name: Agentstools Drug Interactions
description: Fetch the drug-interactions section of an FDA drug label by drug name, with an optional check of whether that label mentions a second drug. Powered by openFDA — a label-text heuristic, informational, not medical advice. Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params. Required: drug (string — primary drug brand, generic or ingredient name). Optional: interacts_with (string — a second drug to check for a mention in the first drug's interactions section). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { query {drug (string), interacts_with (string|null)}, found (bool — whether a matching label interactions section was found), interactions (object|null — the label interactions text, e.g. {truncated (bool), source_tag: 'drug_interactions'}), interaction_check {interacts_with (string), mentioned_in_label (bool — label-text heuristic), note (string)}, sources {errors {} , partial (bool), providers[] (e.g. ['drug_label'])}, attribution[] (e.g. ['openFDA, U.S. Food & Drug Administration ...']), disclaimer (string) }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/interactions?drug=<name> with optional &interacts_with=<second drug name> — both params are query-string, only drug is required, no request body. x402 paid endpoint, $0.02 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. query echoes the parsed drug + interacts_with. found signals whether a matching FDA label interactions section was located; interactions carries that section's text (truncated flag + source_tag) when present. interaction_check.mentioned_in_label is a boolean label-text heuristic — true only means the first drug's interactions section literally mentions the second drug's name, NOT a clinical interaction determination (see interaction_check.note). sources.providers lists the upstream sources drawn on (drug_label), sources.partial/errors flag any upstream fetch problems, and attribution[]/disclaimer carry the openFDA licensing + not-medical-advice notes.
quirks: Only `drug` is required; `interacts_with` is an optional query param — there is no request body.

interaction_check.mentioned_in_label is a LABEL-TEXT HEURISTIC (does the first drug's interactions section mention the second drug's name), NOT a clinical interaction assessment — the endpoint says so explicitly in interaction_check.note and the disclaimer.
Powered by openFDA (open.fda.gov) drug-label data; informational aggregation of public FDA data, not medical advice, not a diagnosis, no FDA endorsement.

Upstream openFDA (api.fda.gov) can transiently rate-limit/403 — when it does, the endpoint still returns HTTP 200 but with found=false, interactions=null, sources.partial=true and sources.errors.drug_label describing the upstream status; retry for full data.
Price $0.02 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key. The x402 quote lives in the base64 'payment-required' response header, not the JSON body (body is empty {}).
usage.guide: Look up the drug-interactions section of an FDA drug label by drug name, and optionally check whether that label mentions a specific second drug. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/drug/interactions with the required `drug` param (brand, generic or ingredient name) and the optional `interacts_with` param (a second drug name). It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.02 USDC on Base; no API key, synchronous, no polling. Read `found` to see if a label interactions section was located, `interactions` for that section's text, and `interaction_check.mentioned_in_label` for whether the second drug is named in the first drug's interactions section — but treat that boolean as a label-text heuristic, not a clinical interaction determination (see interaction_check.note and the disclaimer; consult a licensed professional and the FDA label before acting). Data is powered by openFDA; sources.partial/sources.errors flag any upstream FDA fetch problems. Verified 2026-07-31 with {drug:'warfarin', interacts_with:'aspirin'} -> HTTP 200, $0.02 charged on Base; on that call upstream api.fda.gov transiently returned 403 (found=false, sources.partial=true) but the endpoint returned its full structured envelope.

name: Agentstools Entity Search
description: Disambiguate a company by name — fuzzy legal-name search returning ranked candidate entities, each cross-linked to its public reference ids (Wikidata QID, GLEIF LEI, SEC CIK, stock ticker), country and a match score.

name.description: Company name to search for (required)

source.description: Which registry the candidate came from: sec | gleif | wikidata

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/entity/search with query params: name (REQUIRED company name string), country (OPTIONAL country filter e.g. US), limit (OPTIONAL integer 1-10, default 5). No request body. Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: query (echoed name); count; candidates[].{name,qid(Wikidata QID or null),lei(GLEIF LEI or null),cik(SEC CIK or null),ticker(or null),country(or null),jurisdiction(or null),score(0-100 fuzzy match),source(sec|gleif|wikidata)}; sources.{errors,partial}; disclaimer; attribution[].
quirks: All input is query params (name required); no request body. An empty name returns HTTP 400.

Candidates are pooled across THREE public registries (SEC EDGAR, GLEIF LEI, Wikidata) and ranked by a 0-100 fuzzy match score; each candidate's `source` field says which registry it came from, and id fields not known to that source are null (e.g. a Wikidata hit has a qid but null lei/cik/ticker).

Same real-world company can appear as multiple candidates from different sources (e.g. name=Apple returned both a SEC row with cik=0000320193/ticker=AAPL and a Wikidata row with qid=Q312 for 'Apple Inc.'). Cross-link by legal name to assemble the full id bundle.
Without a country filter results span jurisdictions and include non-corporate hits (name=Apple surfaced Apple Music and generic Wikidata items). Use the country param to narrow.

This is the CHEAP disambiguation step — the provider's disclaimer points at a downstream /entity/resolve for a verified single-entity resolution. Business-entity reference data only; provider labels output as fuzzy candidates, not legal/investment/compliance advice.
Returns partial results (sources.partial=true, sources.errors populated) when one upstream registry is briefly down rather than failing the whole call.
usage.guide: Disambiguate a company name into ranked candidate entities with their public reference ids in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/entity/search?name=<company>&limit=5 (optionally &country=US). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns candidates[] ranked by fuzzy score, each carrying whatever ids are known for it — Wikidata QID, GLEIF LEI, SEC CIK, stock ticker — plus country and the source registry (sec|gleif|wikidata). Use it to map a free-text company name to canonical ids before pulling filings/financials, or as the cheap first step before /entity/resolve. Verified live: name=Apple&limit=5 returned 5 ranked candidates including the SEC row (Apple Inc., cik=0000320193, ticker=AAPL, US, score=66.7) and Wikidata Q312.

name: Agentstools KYB Screen
description: Fuzzy-screen a company name against the GLEIF LEI business registry and get back ranked candidate entities, each with its LEI, legal name, jurisdiction, registration status and corroboration level.

name.description: Company name to screen for (required)

country.description: Optional ISO country filter, e.g. US

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/kyb/screen with query params: name (REQUIRED company name string), country (OPTIONAL ISO country filter e.g. US), limit (OPTIONAL integer 1-10, default 5). No request body. Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: query (echoed name); count; candidates[].{lei,legal_name,jurisdiction,country,registration_status(ISSUED|LAPSED|RETIRED|ANNULLED|MERGED...),entity_status(ACTIVE...),corroboration_level(FULLY_CORROBORATED|PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED...),score(0-100 fuzzy match)}; sources.{errors,partial}; attribution[]; disclaimer.
