This is the CHEAP first step of a two-step KYB flow — screen (this endpoint) to disambiguate the entity, then call /kyb/verify with a precise LEI for the full legitimacy verdict.

candidates are ranked by a fuzzy match score; without a country filter results span jurisdictions (e.g. name=Apple surfaced entities in FR/IN/BE, not only Apple Inc.). Use the country param to narrow.
Returns a partial result (sources.partial=true, sources.errors populated) when the GLEIF source is briefly down rather than failing.

Business-entity metadata only, never data about individuals. Source is the GLEIF LEI Golden Copy (CC0), enriched with SEC EDGAR (public domain) and Wikidata (CC0). Provider labels the output as legitimacy indicators, not legal/credit/compliance advice.
usage.guide: Screen a company name against the GLEIF LEI business registry in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/kyb/screen?name=<company>&limit=5 (optionally &country=US). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns ranked candidate entities, each with its LEI, legal name, jurisdiction/country, registration_status, entity_status, GLEIF corroboration_level and a fuzzy match score — the cheap disambiguation step before calling /kyb/verify with a precise LEI. Verified live: name=Apple&limit=5 returned 5 ranked GLEIF candidates (top: APPLE 12, LEI 969500RDBEVTUKOLE690, FR, score 76.9).

name: X402node Lead Enrichment
description: One-call B2B lead enrichment for a company: scrapes the company website and contact page for contact emails and social profiles, then pulls a name-matched local business record (phone, address, rating, category) from maps, returning a single structured lead.

domain.description: Company website domain, e.g. stripe.com (recommended). Passed as a query param.

company.description: Company name, used for the local/maps lookup. Optional if domain is given. Passed as a query param.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/app/lead-enrich?domain=<domain>&company=<name> (x402 Base or Solana USDC, no body). Both are query params; pass domain (recommended) and/or company (used for the maps lookup). At least one is needed. Pay the fixed $0.10 x402 quote and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON (from the paid 200): { company:'Stripe', domain:'stripe.com', siteTitle:null, emails:[...contact emails scraped from the site/contact page], socials:{...social profile URLs}, headings:[...], local:{ name:'Stripe Toronto Office', address:'1 University Ave, Toronto, ON M5J 1S8, Canada', phone:null, rating:3.1, category:'Business development service', link:'https://www.google.com/maps/place/...' }, localNote:null, pagesScraped:['https://stripe.com'], note: string, source:'brightdata+serp', _hint: promo string }.
quirks: Both inputs are query params (domain, company), never a body. Provide domain (recommended) and/or company; company is used for the local/maps lookup and is optional if domain is given.
Fixed price ($0.10 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 100000-atomic live 402 accept) - not a dynamic quote.
Live 402 advertises BOTH a Base (eip155:8453 USDC) and a Solana (USDC) accept at the same 100000-atomic amount; either network works. Paid via Base.

emails/socials/headings are best-effort scrapes and can come back empty when the site blocks scraping or exposes no contact addresses (they were empty for stripe.com in the verified call), while the maps-sourced local business record (name/address/rating/category/link) was still returned.
local is a single best name-matched Google Maps business record (may be a regional office, e.g. 'Stripe Toronto Office' for company=Stripe); use company + domain together to improve the match.
source is 'brightdata+serp' (residential-IP website scraping + SERP/maps aggregation). Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.
usage.guide: Enrich a company into a single structured B2B lead in one paid call. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/app/lead-enrich?domain=<domain>&company=<name> (e.g. domain=stripe.com&company=Stripe) with no body, and pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.10 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `emails` and `socials` are contact emails + social profiles scraped from the company website/contact page (can be empty when the site blocks scraping), and `local` is a name-matched Google Maps business record (name/address/phone/rating/category/link). `pagesScraped` lists the URLs hit and `source` records the pipeline. Synchronous - no polling.

name: x402node Company Intelligence
description: One-call company intelligence for a domain: RDAP registration (age, registrar, expiry, status), DNS (MX records, mail-provider guess, A-records, nameservers), a live website HEAD check (server, status, final URL), and a Wikipedia company summary. For company info, domain lookup, lead enrichment, and due diligence.

domain.description: Company domain to look up, e.g. stripe.com. A leading http(s):// and www. are accepted. Alias: d. Passed as a query param.

wiki.description: Optional. Exact Wikipedia article title for a better company-summary match, e.g. 'Stripe, Inc.'. Defaults to the domain name. Alias: name.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/finance/company?domain=<domain> (x402 Base or Solana USDC, no body). domain is a query param (alias: d); optional wiki=<exact Wikipedia title> (alias: name) improves the company-summary match. Pay the fixed $0.004 x402 quote and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON (from the paid 200): { domain:'stripe.com', registration:{ available, created:'1995-09-12T04:00:00Z', expires, last_changed, age_years:30.9, registrar:'SafeNames Ltd.', status:[...] }, dns:{ has_email:true, mx_records:['aspmx.l.google.com',...], mail_provider_guess:'Google Workspace', a_records:['198.202.176.41',...], nameservers:[...] }, website:{ online:true, status:200, server:'nginx', final_url:'https://stripe.com/' }, wikipedia:{ found:false } (adds a summary when a matching article is found), source:'RDAP + DNS(Google DoH) + Wikipedia + live HEAD', note: string, _hint: promo string }.
quirks: domain is passed as a query param (alias d), never a body; a leading http(s):// and www. are stripped automatically.
Fixed price ($0.004 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 4000-atomic live 402 accept) - not a dynamic quote.
Live 402 advertises BOTH a Base (eip155:8453 USDC) and a Solana (USDC) accept at the same 4000-atomic amount; either network works. Paid via Base.
wikipedia.found is false when no matching article is located (Wikipedia lookup missed for stripe.com in the verified call) - pass wiki=<exact article title, e.g. 'Stripe, Inc.'> to improve the match.
registration is RDAP-sourced; dns is resolved via Google DoH; website is a live HEAD check (server/status/final_url); combine them for domain age, mail-provider, and liveness signals.
Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.
usage.guide: Enrich a company from its domain in one paid call. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/finance/company?domain=<domain> (e.g. domain=stripe.com; optionally add wiki=<exact Wikipedia article title> for a better company summary) with no body, and pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.004 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `registration` gives RDAP domain age/registrar/expiry/status, `dns` gives MX records + mail_provider_guess + A-records + nameservers, `website` is a live HEAD check (online/status/server/final_url), and `wikipedia` carries a company summary when found. Synchronous - no polling.

name: Stable Deepline Company Enrich
description: Enrich a company domain (or name / LinkedIn) into a merged 30+ field profile from Apollo, Crustdata, and PeopleDataLabs: revenue, headcount, industry, funding, valuation, tech stack, social profiles, SIC/NAICS codes, and HQ address. Keyless x402, no accounts.

domain.description: Company domain to enrich (for example stripe.com).

company_name.description: Company name fallback when domain is unavailable.

linkedin.description: LinkedIn company page id or full company URL.

usage.callShape: POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/company/enrich with JSON body containing at least one of { domain | company_name | linkedin }. Returns HTTP 200 synchronously with the full profile inline (a job_id is present but the result is already completed -- no polling needed).
usage.outputShape: job_id, status ('completed'), billing.{credits_charged,cost_usd}, result.data.{status,start_date,stop_date,job_id,input.task.{domain,company_name,linkedin,...},output.company.{id,domain,name,website,linkedin_id,description,logo_url,size,employees_count,industry,type,founded,address,country,linkedin_url,linkedin_followers,crunchbase_url,funding_details.{total_funding_rounds,total_funding_usd,funding_rounds[]},recent_job_posting_count,technologies[]}}
quirks: Waterfall enrichment merging Apollo, Crustdata, and PeopleDataLabs into one 30+ field company profile.
Synchronous despite carrying a job_id: the paid 200 already contains status:'completed' with the result inline -- no status endpoint to poll.
Provide at least one of domain (best), company_name, or linkedin (company page id or URL).
Some fields can come back empty/null for a given company (e.g. Stripe returned funding_details with 0 rounds, empty technologies[], and null logo_url) -- coverage depends on the underlying sources.
Fixed price $0.10 (x402, Base USDC); response also echoes a billing block (credits_charged ~0.98, cost_usd ~0.098).
usage.guide: Enrich a company into a merged 30+ field profile (revenue, headcount, industry, funding, valuation, tech stack, social profiles, SIC/NAICS, HQ) from Apollo + Crustdata + PeopleDataLabs. POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/company/enrich with a JSON body containing at least one of { domain | company_name | linkedin }, e.g. {"domain":"stripe.com"}. Pay $0.10 via x402 (Base USDC). Returns HTTP 200 synchronously; read result.data.output.company for the profile fields.

name: Stable Deepline Email From LinkedIn
description: Resolve a LinkedIn profile URL (/in/ format) into a verified work email via a waterfall search across multiple providers (Findymail, Prospeo, Lusha, ContactOut, Forager, LeadMagic).

inputSchema.linkedin_url: string (required) — standard LinkedIn profile URL in /in/ format, e.g. https://www.linkedin.com/in/satyanadella. Sent as a JSON request body.

outputs.email: { kind, path, value } — value is the resolved work email string (null if none found)
outputs.email_source: { kind, path, value:string } — which waterfall provider produced it (e.g. leadmagic_social_email)
outputs.miss_reason: { kind, path, value:string|null } — reason no email was found

outputSchema.steps: array of per-provider step records { id, kind, status }
outputSchema.logs: { tail:string[], totalCount:number, returnedCount:number } — per-step execution log
outputSchema.next: object of follow-up read commands { inspect, full, billing, logs } with runId + API paths (GET /api/v2/runs/{runId}) for retrieving the full run

usage.callShape: POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/email/from-linkedin with JSON body {"linkedin_url":"https://www.linkedin.com/in/<handle>"} (must be a standard /in/ profile URL). Pay $0.17 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the completed run is returned inline in the 200, no polling.
usage.outputShape: Result is a 'play_run' envelope. Read the answer from outputs.*.value: outputs.email.value (the work email string, or null), outputs.email_found_and_valid.value (bool), outputs.email_validated.value (bool), outputs.email_source.value (which waterfall provider found it, e.g. leadmagic_social_email), outputs.miss_reason.value (why nothing was found, null on success). run.status is 'completed'; logs.tail[] shows each provider probed. Observed: satyanadella -> outputs.email.value='satya@microsoft.com', email_found_and_valid=true, source leadmagic_social_email.
quirks: linkedin_url must be a standard /in/ profile URL; the waterfall (Findymail, Prospeo, Lusha, ContactOut, Forager, LeadMagic) targets WORK email, not personal — for personal email/phone from a LinkedIn URL use a different op.
The real answer is nested: read outputs.email.value (the flat top-level 'email' key does NOT exist; every field is wrapped in { kind, path, value }).
A valid 200 can still return outputs.email.value=null with email_found_and_valid=false and a miss_reason — pay does not guarantee a hit; gate on email_found_and_valid + email_validated.
Fixed price $0.17 (openapi x-payment-info and the live 402 agree: amount 170000 = 0.17 USDC, 6 decimals, Base only — no Solana accept offered).
Response also carries a 'next' block of deepline runs get / GET /api/v2/runs/{runId} commands to re-fetch the full run, inspection, or billing after the fact (not required to read the result).
usage.guide: Find a person's verified work email from their LinkedIn profile URL. POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/email/from-linkedin with JSON body {"linkedin_url":"https://www.linkedin.com/in/<handle>"} (standard /in/ URL). Pay $0.17 USDC via x402 on Base; synchronous (completed run inline in the 200, no poll). The result is a play_run envelope — read outputs.email.value for the email (may be null), outputs.email_found_and_valid.value and outputs.email_validated.value for confidence, outputs.email_source.value for which provider found it, and outputs.miss_reason.value if empty. Runs a multi-provider waterfall (Findymail/Prospeo/Lusha/ContactOut/Forager/LeadMagic) so a paid 200 can still be a miss — always check email_found_and_valid before using the address.

name: Stable Deepline Find Personal Email
description: Find a person's personal email address via a waterfall search (Dropleads, LeadMagic, PeopleDataLabs and more) given their first and last name; best coverage when a LinkedIn URL plus company domain/name is supplied.

outputSchema.description: play_run envelope; the resolved result lives under outputs.*.value

run.description: id, playName, status, startedAt, finishedAt, durationMs

usage.callShape: POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/email/personal with a JSON body { first_name, last_name, linkedin_url?, domain?, company_name? } (x402, Base USDC, no API key). first_name + last_name are required; add linkedin_url (and domain/company_name) for best coverage. Result returns inline in the 200 (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: play_run envelope: { schemaVersion, kind:'play_run', run:{ id, playName, status:'completed', durationMs, ... }, steps:[], outputs:{ personal_email:{value:string|null}, email_found_and_valid:{value:bool}, email_validated:{value:bool}, email_source:{value:string|null}, miss_reason:{value:string|null} }, datasets:[], logs:{tail[],totalCount}, next:{inspect,full,billing,logs} }. Read outputs.personal_email.value for the email and outputs.email_found_and_valid.value to know if a valid personal email was found.
quirks: Result is nested inside a play_run wrapper — the actual email is at outputs.personal_email.value (with outputs.email_found_and_valid.value / outputs.email_validated.value flags), not at the top level.
When nothing is found the call still returns HTTP 200 with personal_email=null and miss_reason (e.g. 'no_valid_personal_email') — a miss is a normal paid success, not an error.
Charge is fixed $0.10 per call whether or not an email is found (verified paid probe on Patrick Collison @ stripe.com returned no personal email — founders' personal emails are rarely in these DBs).

The openapi lists Dropleads/LeadMagic/PeopleDataLabs, but the live run fans out across many more sources (contactout, aviato, limadata, wiza, icypeas, forager, datagma, leadmagic, ...) as a durable waterfall.
Pass first_name + last_name (both required, minLength 1); linkedin_url gives the best coverage per the provider; additionalProperties=false so only the five documented fields are accepted.
usage.guide: Find a person's personal (non-work) email address. POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/email/personal with JSON { first_name, last_name, linkedin_url?, domain?, company_name? } and pay the fixed $0.10 x402 charge (Base USDC, no API key). first_name + last_name are required; supplying a linkedin_url (and domain/company_name) markedly improves coverage. The service runs a synchronous waterfall across many contact-data providers and returns a play_run envelope in the 200; read outputs.personal_email.value for the address and outputs.email_found_and_valid.value / outputs.miss_reason.value to interpret misses. A no-match still costs $0.10 and returns 200 with personal_email=null.

name: Stable Deepline Work Email Finder
description: Find a verified work email from a person's first/last name and company domain — runs a waterfall search across 79+ providers (Apollo, Hunter, Prospeo, and more) plus common email-pattern guesses, stopping at the first provider that returns a validated hit. Keyless x402 (no API key).

linkedin_url.description: Optional standard LinkedIn profile URL — enables LinkedIn-native fallback providers.

outputSchema.description: play_run envelope. The resolved email lives at outputs.email.value; outputs.email_source.value names the winning provider/pattern; outputs.email_validated.value is a boolean.

usage.callShape: POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/email/work with JSON body {first_name, last_name, domain, company_name?, linkedin_url?}. Single x402 payment (Base USDC, ~$0.04), no API key. Synchronous — the result is returned inline in the 200 response; no polling required.
usage.outputShape: JSON play_run envelope. Read the found email at outputs.email.value (e.g. "patrick@stripe.com"), the discovery method at outputs.email_source.value (e.g. "pattern_first_at", or a provider name like hunter/prospeo), and whether it was verified at outputs.email_validated.value (boolean). run.{status,durationMs} give run metadata; steps[] + logs.tail[] show which of the 79+ providers/patterns were tried; next.{inspect,full,billing,logs} carry follow-up GET routes for the run id.
quirks: first_name, last_name, and domain are all REQUIRED; company_name and linkedin_url are optional hints (linkedin_url enables LinkedIn-native fallback providers).
domain must be a bare company domain (e.g. acme.com), not a full URL or an @-prefixed address.

Waterfall design: it tries email-pattern guesses (pattern_first_at, pattern_flast, pattern_first_dot_last, ...) then paid providers (Hunter, LeadMagic, Prospeo, FullEnrich, Lusha, ContactOut, ...) and stops at the first validated hit — a single flat $0.04 covers the whole run regardless of how many providers it consults.
Fixed price ($0.04) whether or not an email is found; a miss returns the play_run envelope with an empty/absent outputs.email.value.
Synchronous — the run completes within the request (observed ~7.6s) and the answer is inline in the 200; the next.* GET routes are optional for re-inspecting the run, not required to get the result.
usage.guide: Use to find a verified work email when you already know a person's name and their employer's domain. Send POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/email/work with {first_name, last_name, domain} (optionally company_name and linkedin_url to widen provider coverage). Keyless x402 on Base (~$0.04 flat per call). Read outputs.email.value for the email, outputs.email_validated.value to confirm it was verified, and outputs.email_source.value for how it was found. The call is synchronous — no polling. Price is the same on a miss, so only call when you have a real name + domain.

name: Stable Deepline Person From Email
description: Reverse a business/work email address (or a LinkedIn profile URL) into the person behind it: name, title, headline, company/employment history, education, location, and canonical LinkedIn URL. Keyless x402 (Base USDC), synchronous result inline. Personal webmail domains (e.g. gmail.com) are rejected.

inputSchema.description: Provide at least one of email or linkedin_url.

email.description: Business/work email address to enrich. Personal webmail domains such as gmail.com are rejected.

outputSchema.description: job_id + status ('completed') + result.data[] person records + billing.

usage.callShape: POST https://stable-deepline.dev/api/person/from-email with a JSON body containing at least one of { "email" } (a business/work email; webmail like gmail.com is rejected) or { "linkedin_url" }. One x402 payment (Base USDC $0.12, no API key). Returns 200 inline with { job_id, status:"completed", result.data[], billing } — no polling.
usage.outputShape: { job_id, status:"completed", result: { data: [ { name, title, headline, summary, location, email, linkedin_flagship_url, linkedin_profile_url, profile_picture_url, num_of_connections, all_employers[], current_employers[{employer_name, employee_title, start_date, end_date, domains[]}], past_employers[], education_background[{institute_name, degree_name, field_of_study}], all_titles[], all_schools[], person_id } ] }, billing: { credits_charged, cost_usd } }
quirks: Synchronous: returns 200 with result inline (status:"completed") — unlike the play-backed Deepline routes (contacts/by-role, email/work, email/from-linkedin, email/personal, phone/find, linkedin/find, person/job-change) this enrichment route is NOT subject to the shared ~5-concurrency play pool and does not queue.
Personal webmail domains (gmail.com, etc.) are rejected — pass a work/business email or a linkedin_url.
Underlying data source is Crustdata (response returns crustdata-media S3 permalinks + a Crustdata person_id).
Verified with a well-known public LinkedIn URL (williamhgates -> Bill Gates); returned full profile + employment history.
Fixed price $0.12 per call regardless of hit/miss; billing.cost_usd echoes the charge.
usage.needs: At least one of a business/work email address or a LinkedIn profile URL.
usage.guide: Best for reversing a known work email (or LinkedIn URL) into an enriched person profile — name, current title/headline, full employment and education history, and canonical LinkedIn URL. Use { "email": "<work email>" } when you have an email; use { "linkedin_url": "<profile url>" } when you have a profile link. Do NOT pass personal webmail (gmail/outlook/yahoo) — it is rejected. Result is returned inline in one call; no polling. For finding an email from a name+domain use the sibling Stable Deepline email routes instead.

name: OpenWebNinja Email Search
description: Search the web for email addresses associated with a domain by keyword query — returns a list of crawled email addresses matching the given company/keyword and email domain.

query.description: Keyword / company name to search the web for email addresses. Required.

email_domain.description: The email domain to restrict results to, e.g. 'microsoft.com'. Required.

limit.description: Maximum number of email addresses to return.

data.description: List of email addresses matching the query + email_domain.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/email-search/search-emails?query=<keyword/company>&email_domain=<domain>&limit=<n> — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, Polygon, or Arbitrum). The email list is returned inline in the 200 JSON under data[]; no polling.
usage.outputShape: { status:'OK', request_id, data:[ '<email>', ... ] } — data is a flat array of email-address strings. Verified with query='Microsoft'&email_domain='microsoft.com'&limit=20 → HTTP 200, data included e.g. 'billg@microsoft.com', 'scottgu@microsoft.com', 'familysafety@microsoft.com', 'no-reply-powerbi@microsoft.com' (some partially masked like 'nn...@microsoft.com').
quirks: BOTH query and email_domain are required — omitting either yields a validation error, not a paid empty result. query is a keyword/company name; email_domain constrains results to that domain (e.g. 'microsoft.com').
limit is optional (default 5000); it caps how many addresses come back in data[].
data[] is a flat list of email-address STRINGS (not objects) — no name/title/verification metadata; some addresses are partially masked (e.g. 'nn...@microsoft.com').
Results are crawled from the web index, so coverage and freshness vary by domain; a valid call can legitimately return an empty data[] for an obscure domain.
Flat price $0.003 per call (amount 3000, USDC 6dp); the live 402 quotes Base, Polygon, and Arbitrum (the exact amount is always in the endpoint's own 402 challenge).
Only exposed at /email-search/search-emails — no short-alias or namespaced duplicate in this provider sweep.
usage.guide: Discover email addresses for an organization/domain from the web. GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/email-search/search-emails with query params: ?query=<keyword or company name, required, e.g. 'Microsoft'>, &email_domain=<domain to restrict to, required, e.g. 'microsoft.com'>, &limit=<max addresses, optional, default 5000>. Pay per call via x402 (flat $0.003 USDC on Base, Polygon, or Arbitrum; no API key, no account). Read the results from data[] — a flat array of email-address strings (some may be partially masked). Result is synchronous in the 200; no polling. Use this for lead-gen / contact discovery by domain; for resolving one specific person's email from their name, prefer a targeted email-finder instead. Verified 2026-08-07 with query='Microsoft'&email_domain='microsoft.com' → HTTP 200, $0.003 charged.

name: OpenWebNinja Job Salary
aka: job salary by title and location
description: Estimate salaries/pay for a job title in a given location — returns min/median/max total compensation plus base-salary and additional-pay breakdowns, the salary period, currency, sample size, last-updated timestamp, the data publisher and a confidence level, refinable by location type and years of experience.

job_title.description: Job title for which to get salary estimation (e.g. 'nodejs developer').

location.description: Free-text location/area in which to get salary estimation (e.g. 'new york').

location_type.description: Type of the location, for additional accuracy.

years_of_experience.description: Restrict the estimate to a specific experience-level range (years).

items.description: Salary record: location, job_title, min_salary, max_salary, median_salary, min_base_salary, max_base_salary, median_base_salary, min_additional_pay, max_additional_pay, median_additional_pay, salary_period, salary_currency, salary_count, salaries_updated_at, publisher_name, publisher_link, confidence.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/job-salary-data/job-salary?job_title=<title>&location=<place> — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum). The estimate is returned inline in the 200 JSON under data[]; no polling.
usage.outputShape: { status:'OK', request_id, data:[ { location, job_title, min_salary, max_salary, median_salary, min_base_salary, max_base_salary, median_base_salary, min_additional_pay, max_additional_pay, median_additional_pay, salary_period, salary_currency, salary_count, salaries_updated_at, publisher_name, publisher_link, confidence } ] }. Verified with job_title='nodejs developer', location='new york' → HTTP 200: one entry, location 'New York, NY', job_title 'Nodejs Developer', min_salary 120296.11, median_salary 154014.13, max_salary 199160.95, base median 125445.72, additional median 28568.41, salary_period YEAR, salary_currency USD, salary_count 6, salaries_updated_at 2025-04-10T23:59:59Z, publisher_name 'Glassdoor', confidence CONFIDENT.
quirks: job_title and location are the two required query params; location is free-text and accepts a city/state/country (e.g. 'new york').

Refine accuracy with optional params: location_type (ANY|CITY|STATE|COUNTRY, default ANY) and years_of_experience (ALL|LESS_THAN_ONE|ONE_TO_THREE|FOUR_TO_SIX|SEVEN_TO_NINE|TEN_TO_FOURTEEN|ABOVE_FIFTEEN, default ALL).

The live response returns MORE fields than the openapi/402 schema advertises: alongside min/max/median_salary it also includes base-salary (min/max/median_base_salary), additional-pay/bonus (min/max/median_additional_pay), salary_count (sample size) and salaries_updated_at — read those too.
publisher_name reports the underlying source (Glassdoor in the verified call) with a publisher_link; confidence (e.g. CONFIDENT) reflects data reliability.

Flat price $0.003 per call (amount 3000, USDC 6dp), quoted identically in the 402 across Base/Polygon/Arbitrum; the exact amount is always in the endpoint's own 402 challenge (header lists 3 networks, body lists Base+Polygon).

OVERLAPS the existing 'OpenWebNinja Estimated Salary' (/jsearch/estimated-salary) and 'OpenWebNinja Glassdoor Salary Estimate' (/realtime-jobs-data/glassdoor/salary-estimation): all three estimate pay by title+location and can surface Glassdoor-sourced numbers. This '/job-salary-data/job-salary' is OpenWeb Ninja's standalone Job Salary Data API product — indexed as distinct, but a curate may choose to dedupe against the JSearch estimated-salary op (near-identical response; values differed only ~0.1% at index time).
Sibling /job-salary-data/company-job-salary is a DISTINCT op (salary by company + title) — not an alias; /job-salary-data/job-salary is the canonical, alias-free path in this sweep.
usage.guide: Estimate pay for a role in a place. GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/job-salary-data/job-salary with query params: ?job_title=<role, required, e.g. 'nodejs developer'>, &location=<place, required, free-text city/state/country, e.g. 'new york'>, and optional &location_type=<ANY|CITY|STATE|COUNTRY, default ANY>, &years_of_experience=<ALL|LESS_THAN_ONE|ONE_TO_THREE|FOUR_TO_SIX|SEVEN_TO_NINE|TEN_TO_FOURTEEN|ABOVE_FIFTEEN, default ALL>. Pay per call via x402 (flat $0.003 USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum; no API key, no account). Read the estimate from data[] — total pay (min_salary/max_salary/median_salary), base pay (min/max/median_base_salary), additional pay/bonus (min/max/median_additional_pay), plus salary_period, salary_currency, salary_count (sample size), salaries_updated_at, publisher_name/publisher_link and confidence. Result is synchronous in the 200; no polling. Verified 2026-08-07 with job_title='nodejs developer', location='new york' → HTTP 200, $0.003 charged, median total $154,014/yr (Glassdoor, CONFIDENT).

name: OpenWebNinja Zillow Agent Search
description: Search Zillow real-estate agents by location (city-state slug), optionally filtered by name, returning agent/team profiles with review ratings, sales stats, brokerage, profile links, and an encodedZuid identifier for follow-up agent-listing lookups.

location.description: Location slug for the agent search in city-state format, e.g. 'new-york-ny', 'los-angeles-ca', 'miami-fl'. Required.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Each page returns up to 15 agents.

name.description: Optional filter to restrict results to agents matching this name.

parameters.description: Echo of the resolved query params: { location, name, page }.

items.description: cardTitle, secondaryCardTitle (brokerage), cardActionLink (Zillow profile URL), encodedZuid, imageUrl, logoUrl, isTopAgent, profileData[] ({formattedData,label} pairs e.g. price range / sales last 12 months / sales in <state>), reviewInformation ({reviewAverage, reviewAverageText, reviewCountFormattedText, noReviewsText}), tags[] ({__typename, tagType, text} e.g. TEAM).

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/realtime-real-estate-data/zillow/agent-search?location=<city-state slug>&page=<n>&name=<optional> — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, Polygon, or Arbitrum). Results are returned inline in the 200 JSON under data.agents[]; no polling.

name: OpenWebNinja Website Contacts Scraper

query.description: Domain (or any valid URL, root domain is used) to scrape emails and contacts from (e.g. 'wsgr.com'). Supports batching up to 20 domains separated by comma (e.g. 'wsgr.com,other.com') — each domain consumes a request credit. Required.

match_email_domain.description: Only return emails whose domain (after the '@') matches the queried domain.

external_matching.description: Also try to match contacts from any web source, in addition to the website and its social platforms.

data.description: One object per queried domain; each has domain, query, emails[{value, sources[]}], phone_numbers[{value, sources[]}], and social profile URL strings (or null): facebook, instagram, tiktok, snapchat, twitter, linkedin, github, youtube, pinterest.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/website-contacts-scraper/scrape-contacts?query=<domain>[&match_email_domain=true&external_matching=true] — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum). All inputs are query params; no request body. Results are returned inline in the 200 JSON; no polling.
usage.outputShape: { status:'OK', request_id, data:[ { domain, query, emails:[{ value, sources:[url] }], phone_numbers:[{ value, sources:[url] }], facebook, instagram, tiktok, snapchat, twitter, linkedin, github, youtube, pinterest } ] }. Social fields are a profile URL string or null. Verified with query='example.org' -> HTTP 200, one domain object with emails (e.g. office@example.org + sources) and twitter https://twitter.com/example_academy.
quirks: query is the ONLY required param and takes a domain or any URL (its root domain is used as the starting point). Batch up to 20 domains comma-separated (e.g. 'wsgr.com,other.com') — EACH domain consumes a request credit (so a 20-domain call costs 20x).

By default emails are NOT restricted to the queried domain (after the '@') — set match_email_domain=true to return only same-domain emails. Set external_matching=true to also pull contacts from any web source beyond the site and its social profiles.

emails[] and phone_numbers[] items each carry a sources[] array of the URLs where the value was found; the 9 social fields (facebook, instagram, tiktok, snapchat, twitter, linkedin, github, youtube, pinterest) are each a URL string or null.

Flat price $0.003 per call (amount 3000, USDC 6dp), quoted identically in the 402 across Base (eip155:8453), Polygon (eip155:137) and Arbitrum (eip155:42161); payTo 0x3e7c9cA818f713F19e126E3B7B37B47dC1411570. The exact amount is always in the endpoint's own 402 challenge.
VERIFIED via one paid 200 call; per the pay-once policy the call was not repeated.
usage.guide: Extract contact info from a website. GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/website-contacts-scraper/scrape-contacts with ?query=<domain-or-url> (required; e.g. 'wsgr.com'). Add &match_email_domain=true to keep only emails on the queried domain, and &external_matching=true to also search other web sources. Batch up to 20 domains by comma-separating them in query (each domain is billed as one credit). Pay per call via x402 (flat $0.003 USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum; no API key). Read results from data[]: one object per domain with emails[{value,sources}], phone_numbers[{value,sources}], and social profile URLs (facebook/instagram/tiktok/snapchat/twitter/linkedin/github/youtube/pinterest, each a URL or null). name: Agentstools Entity Resolve
description: Resolve one legal entity across three public registries (SEC EDGAR, GLEIF LEI, Wikidata) from a single identifier — pass exactly one of name/ticker/cik/lei/qid/isin and get the reconciled id bundle (CIK, LEI, QID, ISIN, ticker, EIN) plus legal name, jurisdiction, status, per-id provenance, a match block, and an optional GLEIF parent/child hierarchy.

name.description: Legal or common company name (fuzzy match)

country.description: Optional country hint for disambiguation, e.g. US

include.description: Optional extras. Use hierarchy for GLEIF parents and children

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/entity/resolve with query params. Supply EXACTLY ONE primary identifier: name (fuzzy company name), ticker (e.g. AAPL), cik (SEC EDGAR, any zero-padding), lei (20-char GLEIF), qid (Wikidata, e.g. Q312) or isin (12-char). Optional: country (disambiguation hint) and include=hierarchy (adds GLEIF parents/children; also implied when resolving by lei). No request body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: resolved (bool); query.{type,value}; ids.{cik,lei,qid,isin,ticker,ein} (each string or null); entity.{legal_name,jurisdiction,status,registration_status,country}; sources.{provenance (per-id -> which registry: input|sec|gleif|wikidata),errors,partial}; match.{method(deterministic|fuzzy),score(0-100),ambiguous,conflicts[]}; website (or null); disclaimer; attribution[]; hierarchy.{direct_parent(or null),ultimate_parent(or null),direct_children[].{lei,name},direct_children_total} (present when include=hierarchy).
quirks: All input is query params; no request body. Supply EXACTLY ONE primary identifier (name/ticker/cik/lei/qid/isin) — supplying none returns HTTP 400; nothing found returns resolved=false (not an error).

It handles the cross-registry plumbing for you: CIK zero-padding mismatch between SEC and Wikidata, and the GLEIF relationship-graph calls for the hierarchy. The value is the FUSION, not a raw resell.

include=hierarchy adds a GLEIF direct_parent, ultimate_parent and a sample of direct_children (with direct_children_total for the real count); resolving by lei also pulls the hierarchy. Verified live: ticker=AAPL returned 8 direct children (Apple Operations International, Braeburn Capital, Apple Energy LLC, etc.) with direct_children_total=8.
match.method is deterministic when resolved from a hard id, fuzzy when resolved from a name; match.ambiguous/conflicts[] flag when two registries disagree on a hard id.

Business-entity metadata only, never data about private individuals. Sources are US-public-domain / CC0 (SEC EDGAR, GLEIF LEI, Wikidata); the disclaimer states identifiers may lag registry updates and it is not legal/investment/compliance advice.
Returns partial results (sources.partial=true, sources.errors populated) when one upstream registry is briefly down rather than a 500.
This is the fuller RESOLUTION step; the cheaper sibling Agentstools Entity Search does fuzzy name -> ranked candidates when you don't yet have a single identifier.
usage.guide: Reconcile a single legal entity's public identifiers in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/entity/resolve with EXACTLY ONE of ?name= / ?ticker= / ?cik= / ?lei= / ?qid= / ?isin= (optionally &country=US, &include=hierarchy). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns the reconciled id bundle (CIK, LEI, QID, ISIN, ticker, EIN) with per-id provenance, the legal name/jurisdiction/status, a match block, and — with include=hierarchy — the GLEIF parent/child corporate graph. Use it to bridge one identifier you have (e.g. a ticker) to every other id before pulling filings/financials/ownership, or as the resolution step after the cheaper Agentstools Entity Search disambiguates a name. Verified live: ticker=AAPL&include=hierarchy -> Apple Inc. (cik 0000320193, lei HWUPKR0MPOU8FGXBT394, qid Q312, isin US0378331005, ein 94-2404110), deterministic match score 100, 8 direct GLEIF children.

name: Agentstools Phone Intel
description: Phone-number intelligence in one call — validity/possibility check, E.164 plus international/national normalization, line type (mobile, fixed line, VOIP, toll-free, premium-rate), country/region, carrier hint, timezones, and a deterministic 0-100 offline fraud/KYC risk score with band and reasons, all from Google libphonenumber number-plan metadata (no live line status, no owner identity).

number.description: Phone number. E.164 (e.g. +14155552671) or a national number when 'country' is also given.

country.description: Optional ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US, GB, DE) for national-format input.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/phone/intel with query params. Required: number — E.164 (e.g. +14155552671) or a national number when country is also supplied. Optional: country (or its alias region) — ISO-3166 alpha-2 (US, GB, DE) to interpret a national-format number. No request body. Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: valid (bool); possible (bool); e164; international; national; country_code (int); region_code (ISO alpha-2); location; number_type (mobile|fixed_line|voip|toll_free|premium_rate|fixed_line_or_mobile|...); carrier (or null); timezones[]; risk_score (0-100 int); risk_band (low|medium|high); reasons[]; signals[]; flagged_carrier (or null); flagged_prefix (or null); disclaimer.

outputExample.disclaimer: These are automated, OFFLINE numbering-plan risk indicators, NOT a definitive fraud verdict and NOT legal or KYC advice.

quirks: All input is query params; no request body. number is required — omitting it returns HTTP 400. Pass a full E.164 number (with leading +), OR a national number plus country=/region= (ISO alpha-2) so it knows the numbering plan.

Offline metadata only: it uses Google libphonenumber number-plan data. It does NOT check live line status, portability, reassignment, or subscriber identity, and carrier is often null (returned null for the verified +14155552671 example).

risk_score (0-100) with risk_band and reasons[]/signals[] is a DETERMINISTIC offline heuristic (flagged prefix/carrier patterns), explicitly not a definitive fraud verdict or KYC advice per the disclaimer.
number_type distinguishes mobile / fixed_line / voip / toll_free / premium_rate; some plans (e.g. North America) can't separate mobile from fixed line and return fixed_line_or_mobile.
The provider states the input number is not stored.
usage.guide: Validate and profile a phone number in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/phone/intel?number=<E.164> (or ?number=<national>&country=<ISO alpha-2>). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns validity/possibility, E.164 + international/national formatting, country/region, line type, carrier hint, timezones, and a 0-100 offline risk score with band/reasons — from Google libphonenumber number-plan metadata (no live line status or owner identity). Use it to normalize and sanity-check phone inputs, route by line type, or flag obviously-invalid/high-risk numbers before a costlier live lookup. Verified live: number=+14155552671 -> valid=true, e164 +14155552671, region_code US, location San Francisco CA, number_type fixed_line_or_mobile, timezone America/Los_Angeles, risk_score 0 (low).

name: Agentstools Domain Enrich
description: One-call enrichment of a domain, company or email-domain into one aggregated JSON profile from public sources — RDAP/WHOIS registration, DNS (A/AAAA/MX/NS, SPF, DMARC), TLS certificate, homepage metadata (title, description, Open Graph, JSON-LD Organization, social links) and a tech-stack detection. Business/domain data only, no personal data. Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params, no request body. Provide ONE of: domain (string, e.g. 'stripe.com'), url (string — its host is used), or email (string — its domain is used). Optional include (array of enum: 'registration'|'dns'|'tls'|'web'|'tech'; repeated query param, e.g. include=dns&include=tls; default = all blocks).
backends.outputSchema: { domain (string — echoed/derived), queried[] (blocks collected), registration: {created, age_days (int), expires, updated, registrar, statuses[], nameservers[], registered (bool)} | null, dns: {resolves (bool), a[], aaaa[], mx[{preference,exchange}], has_mail (bool), mail_provider, ns[], spf:{present,record,policy}, dmarc:{present,record,policy}} | null, tls: {subject_cn, issuer, not_before, not_after, days_to_expiry (int), expired (bool), san_count (int), san_sample[], valid (bool)} | null, web: {final_url, redirected (bool), http_status (int), server, title, description, lang, canonical, open_graph{}, organization:{name,logo,social[]}, contacts[]} | null, tech: {technologies[], count (int)} | null, summary: {sources_ok (int), sources_requested (int), partial (bool), errors{}} }. Each block is null-on-failure (partial, never 500).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/enrich/domain?domain=<domain> — one of domain / url / email as a query param, optional repeated include=<block>; no request body. x402 paid endpoint, $0.015 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON, one aggregated profile. registration = RDAP/WHOIS (age_days, registrar, expiry, statuses, nameservers); dns = A/AAAA/MX (with mail_provider classification), NS, SPF & DMARC policy; tls = live-handshake cert (issuer, validity window, days_to_expiry, SANs); web = homepage metadata (final_url, http_status, title, description, Open Graph, JSON-LD organization name/logo/social links, role contacts); tech = lightweight tech-stack detection. summary.sources_ok/sources_requested + partial + errors report per-block success; each block is null on failure (never 500). Example (domain='stripe.com'): registration.registrar 'SafeNames Ltd.', age_days 11287; dns.mail_provider 'Google Workspace', dmarc.policy 'reject'; tls.issuer 'DigiCert Inc', days_to_expiry 97; web.title 'Stripe | Financial Infrastructure to Grow Your Revenue', organization.name 'Stripe'; tech.technologies ['Nginx','Next.js']; summary.sources_ok 5/5, partial=false.
quirks: Provide exactly one input among domain / url / email as a query param — there is no request body.
include is an OPTIONAL repeated query param (include=dns&include=tls); enum registration|dns|tls|web|tech; omit it to collect all five blocks (the default).

Only PUBLIC business/domain data — RDAP, public DoH resolvers, live TLS handshake, robots-respecting homepage. Personal registrant data is dropped by an allow-list; not a resale of a paid enrichment API.
Partial-friendly: any failing source returns null for that block with summary.partial=true and summary.errors populated — the call never returns HTTP 500. Check summary before trusting a null block.
Price $0.015 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key. The x402 quote lives in the base64 'payment-required' response header, not the JSON body (the 402 body is empty {}).
usage.guide: Enrich a domain, company or email-domain into one aggregated public-data profile in a single call instead of six separate lookups. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/enrich/domain with one of domain, url or email as a query param (e.g. ?domain=stripe.com); optionally add repeated include=<block> params (registration|dns|tls|web|tech) to fetch only some blocks — omit include for all. No request body, no API key. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.015 USDC on Base, synchronous, no polling. Read registration (RDAP/WHOIS age, registrar, expiry, nameservers), dns (A/AAAA/MX with mail-provider classification, NS, SPF, DMARC), tls (cert issuer, validity, days_to_expiry), web (homepage title/description, Open Graph, JSON-LD organization + social links, role contacts) and tech (detected tech stack). Each block is null on upstream failure with summary.partial=true and summary.errors, so the call never 500s — check summary to distinguish a genuine empty from a transient miss. Business/domain data only, never personal data of individuals. Verified 2026-08-07 with {domain:'stripe.com'} -> HTTP 200 in the documented shape, all 5 sources OK, $0.015 charged on Base.

name: Agentstools Litigation Search
description: Find US court cases, opinions and dockets naming a business entity — normalized records with case name, court, date, citation, docket number and nature of suit plus a total match count, sourced live from CourtListener (public-domain).

name.description: Business entity / party name to search (e.g. Apple Inc)

cik.description: Optional SEC CIK id hint to disambiguate the entity

qid.description: Optional Wikidata QID id hint to disambiguate the entity

type.description: Record type: o = opinions (default), r = RECAP dockets, d = dockets

count.description: Total matching records across the source

returned.description: Number of records returned in this page

url.description: Public courtlistener.com link to the opinion/docket

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/legal/litigation with query params: name (business entity / party name; REQUIRED in practice — empty returns HTTP 400), type (OPTIONAL record type enum o=opinions default | r=RECAP dockets | d=dockets), limit (OPTIONAL integer 1-25, default 10), cik / qid (OPTIONAL SEC CIK / Wikidata QID id hints to disambiguate). No request body. Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: query.{name,type}; kind (e.g. 'litigation'); count (total matches, e.g. 2253); returned (page size); recent[].{caseName,court,date,citation(or null),docketNumber(or null),natureOfSuit(or null),role(or null),url(courtlistener.com opinion/docket link)}; sources.{errors,partial,rate_limited,providers[]}; disclaimer; attribution[].
quirks: All input is query params (name required); no request body. An empty name returns HTTP 400.
type selects the record class: o = court opinions (default), r = RECAP dockets, d = dockets. The 'o' path returns opinions with citation/docketNumber often null on older/state records.

count is the TOTAL number of matches across CourtListener (e.g. name='Apple Inc' returned count=2253); only `returned` (<= limit, max 25) records come back in `recent[]`. There is no offset/pagination param — narrow with cik/qid or a more specific name.

Party matching is name-based and can surface both directions of a caption (Apple as plaintiff or defendant) and duplicate opinions for the same docket; filter recent[] by the party/role you care about.
Public-records aggregation for informational due-diligence only — the provider's disclaimer states it is not legal advice and not an FCRA consumer report.
sources.partial / sources.rate_limited flag when the upstream (CourtListener) was briefly degraded rather than failing the whole call.
usage.guide: Search US federal/state court cases, opinions and dockets that name a business entity, for litigation monitoring and KYB/due-diligence. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/legal/litigation?name=<entity>&limit=10 (optionally &type=o|r|d for opinions/RECAP-dockets/dockets, &cik=<SEC CIK> or &qid=<Wikidata QID> to disambiguate). Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 on Base — no API key or account. Returns a total match count plus recent[] records (case name, court, date, citation, docket number, nature of suit, and a public courtlistener.com link). Verified live: name='Apple Inc'&limit=10 -> HTTP 200, $0.03 charged (tx 0x10a2957dbb934135c2416de58a11281d93ff5c8dc4ce32300ad1c84d5efe8f2a), count=2253 with 10 opinions returned including 'Bodenburg v. Apple Inc.' (9th Cir., 2025-07-23) and 'Softview LLC v. Apple Inc.' (Fed. Cir., 2024-07-26).

name: Agentstools Legal Profile
description: One-call composite legal due-diligence profile of a business entity — litigation (CourtListener), US patent portfolio (USPTO PatentsView) and federal regulatory records (Federal Register) fused into cited records with counts, plus a deterministic 0-100 legal-risk score, band, per-dimension flags and reasons.

name.description: Business entity name (primary identifier).

inventor.description: Optional inventor last name for patents.

agency.description: Optional agency slug filter for regulatory.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/legal/profile with QUERY params (no body): name (required — business entity name); optional assignee, inventor, agency, cik, qid, limit (1-25, default 10). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.06 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: query (echo), litigation {count, returned, recent[]{caseName, court, date, citation, docketNumber, url}}, patents {total, returned, recent[]}, regulatory {count, returned, recent[]{title, type, agency, agencies[], date, abstract, html_url, document_number}}, legal_risk {score 0-100, band (low/medium/high), flags{}, reasons[], signals{litigation_total, litigation_recent, regulatory_total, regulatory_recent, recency_years}}, sources {errors{}, partial, rate_limited}, disclaimer, attribution[]. Verified paid response for 'Apple Inc': litigation.count 2253, regulatory.count 2693, patents.total 0 (patentsview not configured on this deployment -> sources.partial true), legal_risk.score 100 band 'high'.
quirks: All params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.

Composite/fusion op, NOT three raw feeds: it cross-normalizes CourtListener litigation, USPTO PatentsView patents and Federal Register regulatory into one dossier plus a deterministic legal-risk score. Distinct from the sibling single-dimension ops /legal/litigation and /legal/regulatory.

legal_risk scoring is deterministic and data-driven (weights/thresholds in a registry) — identical inputs give identical outputs; patents contribute only as an innovation signal and never raise the risk score.

Partial answers are returned when a source is down/rate-limited/unconfigured (sources.partial=true, per-source note in sources.errors) — never a 500. In the verified run patents came back empty because PatentsView requires a free provider key (X402_PATENTSVIEW_KEY) not set on the deployment.
402 body is empty ({}) — the x402 challenge (accepts + bazaar input/output schema) is carried in the base64 `payment-required` response header, not the body.
Public records about business entities only. Not legal advice and not a consumer report; not for FCRA-regulated eligibility decisions (per the response disclaimer).
usage.guide: Get a one-call composite legal due-diligence profile of a business entity with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/legal/profile with QUERY params: name (required — business entity name), plus optional assignee, inventor, agency, cik, qid, limit (1-25, default 10). Preserve attribution[] and disclaimer — public FDA Data Dashboard data, risk indicators only, NOT legal/regulatory advice. name: Agentstools FEC Committee
description: FEC committee profile for a PAC, Super PAC or candidate committee by committee id or name query — type, party, designation, treasurer, plus per-cycle totals of receipts, disbursements, cash on hand and independent expenditures made supporting or opposing candidates.

q.description: Committee name search query (e.g. actblue). Provide either q or committee_id.

committee_id.description: FEC committee id, e.g. C00401224. Provide either q or committee_id.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/fec/committee with query params: q (committee name search query, e.g. actblue) OR committee_id (FEC committee id, e.g. C00401224). No request body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: found (bool); committee.{committee_id,name,committee_type,designation,party(or null),state,treasurer_name,filing_frequency,cycles[]}; totals[].{cycle,receipts,disbursements,cash_on_hand,individual_contributions,independent_expenditures,coverage_start_date,coverage_end_date} (one row per election cycle); independent_expenditures.{total_amount,record_count,support,oppose,partial}; attribution[]; disclaimer.
quirks: All input is query params; provide q (name search) or committee_id (FEC id like C00401224). No request body.

The x402 quote is delivered in the `payment-required` response HEADER (base64 x402 v2 envelope); the raw 402 body is an empty {} (content-length 2). Payment settled normally on retry — capture accepts from the header, not the body.

totals[] is one row per election cycle covered (verified: q=actblue returned 12 cycles 2004-2026, each with receipts/disbursements/cash_on_hand/individual_contributions and a coverage_start/end date).

independent_expenditures rolls up IE records the committee itself made (support vs oppose split); a contribution-only committee like ActBlue shows all zeros there even though it moves billions in receipts.

Public FEC/OpenFEC disclosure data (api.open.fec.gov, US public domain). Provider disclaimer: for due-diligence/compliance/research only, NOT for soliciting or commercially soliciting donors (52 U.S.C. 30111(a)(4)); informational, not legal or investment advice.
Provider was intermittently flaky at index time (sibling calls returned transient 502s); the first payment attempt did not settle (no charge) and a single retry succeeded with HTTP 200.
usage.guide: Look up a US federal political committee (PAC, Super PAC or candidate committee) in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/fec/committee?q=<committee name> (or ?committee_id=C00401224). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns the committee's identity (id, name, type, designation, party, state, treasurer, filing frequency, cycles), per-cycle financial totals (receipts, disbursements, cash on hand, individual contributions, independent expenditures with coverage dates), and a rollup of independent expenditures it made (support vs oppose). Sourced from FEC/OpenFEC public disclosure data. Verified live: q=actblue resolved committee C00401224 (ACTBLUE, Hybrid PAC, MA) with 12 cycles of totals (e.g. 2024: $3.82B receipts, $3.79B disbursements, $99.9M cash on hand).

name: Agentstools Match Dedupe
description: Deduplicate a list of names or addresses into clusters of likely duplicates — blocks by similarity key, confirms pairwise inside each block, and returns clusters with a canonical representative plus counts of inputs, clusters and duplicates.

items.description: The list of strings to deduplicate

type.description: Entity type selecting the normalization pipeline (default company)

min_score.description: Optional match threshold 0-100 (default is the per-type threshold)

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/match/dedupe with JSON body {items:string[] (required), type?: person|company|address|product|org (default company), min_score?: integer 0-100}. No API key. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453); result returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: object ('match_dedupe'); type (echoed entity type); threshold (per-type match threshold used); summary.{input_count,cluster_count,duplicate_count}; clusters[].{cluster_id,size,canonical_representative,similarity_key,members[].{index,input,canonical}}; phonetic_backend (e.g. jellyfish.metaphone); pack_version; disclaimer.

outputExample.disclaimer: Structural normalization plus fuzzy matching over the caller's own strings: results are similarity indicators for deduplication and record-linkage, NOT authoritative identity resolution and NOT libpostal-grade international address parsing. Review before relying on a match.

usage.quirks: Similarity indicators, NOT authoritative identity resolution and NOT libpostal-grade international address parsing — review before relying on a match. type defaults to company; set it to match your data (person/company/address/product/org) so the right normalization pipeline runs. Each cluster of size>1 is a set of likely duplicates; canonical_representative is the suggested survivor. duplicate_count = input_count - cluster_count. Distinct from the sibling /match/name (pairwise name comparison) and from /entity/resolve|/entity/search (single-entity id reconciliation).
usage.needs: A list of name/address strings (items[]). Optionally the entity type and a min_score threshold.
usage.guide: Deduplicate a batch of free-text names or addresses in one paid call. POST https://api.agentstools.dev/match/dedupe with JSON body {items:[...], type:'company'|'person'|'address'|'product'|'org', min_score?:0-100}. items is the only required field; type defaults to company and picks the normalization pipeline. No API key — pay the $0.02 USDC x402 quote on Base and re-request; the result is inline in the synchronous 200. It blocks candidates by a similarity key then confirms pairwise, returning clusters[] (each with cluster_id, size, canonical_representative, similarity_key and members[].{index,input,canonical}) plus summary.{input_count,cluster_count,duplicate_count}. Use it to collapse a messy list into unique entities before dedup/merge or record-linkage; treat matches as similarity indicators, not authoritative identity resolution. Verified live 2026-08-07 with {items:['Acme Inc','ACME Incorporated','Beta LLC'],type:'company'} -> HTTP 200, $0.02 charged, 3 inputs collapsed into 2 clusters (1 duplicate).

Same-host siblings are DISTINCT ops: /nonprofit/search (name->ranked EIN candidates), /nonprofit/status (crisp IRS exempt-status only), /nonprofit/financials (multi-period 990 numbers only). name: Agentstools Nonprofit Search

state.description: Optional 2-letter US state filter, e.g. NY, CA, DC

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/nonprofit/search with query params: name (REQUIRED organization name string), state (OPTIONAL 2-letter US state filter e.g. DC), ntee (OPTIONAL integer 1-10 NTEE category id), c_code (OPTIONAL 501(c) subsection number e.g. 3), limit (OPTIONAL integer 1-25, default 10). quirks: All input is query params (name required); no request body. The bazaar schema lists GET/HEAD/DELETE as allowed methods but GET is the real call.
